title: Standard Operating Procedure for Investigation of Murder Cases
source: Synthesized from BPR&D Investigation Manual for Homicide Cases, BNSS 2023, and State Police Homicide SOPs

steps.title: FIR Registration & Immediate Crime Scene Protection
steps.description: Upon receipt of information regarding homicide, immediately record the FIR under BNSS Section 173 (formerly CrPC Section 154). The Investigating Officer (IO) must rush to the spot, cordon off the entire crime scene with forensic barricade tape, prevent unauthorized entry of public/media, and log all persons present. Note: Local police station / first responder unit is not present in the registry, hence department_entity_id is set to null.
required_evidence: Copy of recorded FIR with statutory date and hour of recording
Crime scene logbook documenting arrival timestamps and identity of first responders
Initial rough sketch map of the scene prepared by the first responder
steps.condition_to_start: Receipt of information regarding a suspicious death or unlawful killing.
steps.condition_to_complete: FIR registered, crime scene secured, and physical barricades erected.
if_blocked: If the crime scene is in a public thoroughfare with hostile crowds, immediately request additional armed reinforcement from District Police Lines before cordoning.

steps.title: Police Inquest Proceedings & Dead Body Challan
steps.description: Conduct formal inquest proceedings (Panchnama) under BNSS Section 194 (formerly CrPC Section 174) in the presence of two or more respectable inhabitants of the neighborhood. Document the apparent cause of death, exact posture of the corpse, ligature marks, and wounds. Prepare the Dead Body Challan and dispatch the corpse under official police escort for autopsy.
required_evidence: Inquest Report (Panchnama) signed by IO and independent witnesses (Panchas)
Detailed inventory of clothing, jewelry, and personal effects found on the corpse
Dead Body Challan / Forwarding Memo addressed to the Medical Officer
steps.condition_to_start: Crime scene secured and body accessible to the investigating team.
steps.condition_to_complete: Inquest finalized, signed by panchas, and corpse transferred to hospital morgue under police seal.
if_blocked: If the identity of the deceased is unknown, take clear identification photographs, record fingerprints, and issue an all-station missing person broadcast before autopsy.

steps.title: Mandatory Forensic Crime Scene Examination & Evidence Seizure
steps.description: In compliance with BNSS Section 176(3) (mandatory forensic investigation for offenses punishable with 7+ years imprisonment), summon the State FSL mobile forensic van. Ensure scientific collection, labeling, and sealing of biological evidence (bloodstains, hair, tissue), ballistic items (cartridge cases, bullets), weapon impressions, and trace evidence under Seizure Memos.
required_evidence: Seizure memos for blood-stained soil, control soil, biological exhibits, and weapons
High-resolution photographic and videographic documentation of the crime scene from all angles
Forensic scene inspection report signed by the scientific officer
steps.condition_to_start: Forensic science team arrives at the protected crime scene.
steps.condition_to_complete: All physical and trace evidence scientifically lifted, packaged, sealed with official seal, and documented.
if_blocked: If the FSL mobile van is delayed beyond 24 hours, the IO must personally lift and seal volatile blood/trace evidence utilizing standardized forensic evidence collection kits under videography.

steps.title: Medico-Legal Post-Mortem Autopsy Requisition
steps.description: Submit a formal written requisition to the autopsy surgeon / forensic medical examiner to conduct post-mortem examination. Request specific opinion on cause and manner of death, time since death, type of weapon used, and preservation of viscera, blood samples, and clothes for FSL chemical/serological analysis.
required_evidence: Certified Medico-Legal Post-Mortem Autopsy Report
Sealed containers containing preserved viscera, blood on gauze, and clothes of the deceased
Autopsy video recording (mandatory in custodial deaths or unidentified bodies)
steps.condition_to_start: Corpse delivered to hospital morgue along with Inquest papers and Dead Body Challan.
steps.condition_to_complete: Receipt of provisional autopsy opinion and handover of sealed biological exhibits to police escort.
if_blocked: If the medical officer is unable to determine the exact cause of death due to putrefaction, request immediate forwarding of preserved bones/viscera to CFSL for advanced osteological and toxicological analysis.

steps.title: Telecom CDR, Cell Site Analysis & Tower Dump Requisition
steps.description: Issue notices under BNSS Section 94 to Telecom Service Providers to obtain Call Detail Records (CDRs), Subscriber Application Forms (CAF), and IMEI histories of the deceased and suspected individuals. Request Cell Tower Dump records for the crime scene location covering the estimated time of murder.
required_evidence: CAF and CDRs with Cell ID tower locations for deceased and suspect mobile numbers
Tower dump logs of all active cellular devices at the crime scene during the occurrence window
Section 63 Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA) electronic certificates from TSP nodal officers
steps.condition_to_start: Deceased's mobile number identified or estimated time of murder established from autopsy.
steps.condition_to_complete: Receipt of certified CDRs, tower dumps, and subscriber KYC from telecom operators.
if_blocked: If suspects utilized encrypted VoIP applications (WhatsApp/Signal) instead of cellular calls, serve Section 94 notices on messaging intermediaries under entity_id meta_platforms for IP access logs.

steps.title: CCTV Surveillance Footage Procurement
steps.description: Identify all private residential, commercial, and municipal CCTV cameras covering the crime scene, approach roads, and escape routes. Issue immediate Section 94 BNSS notices to premises owners or municipal control rooms to procure unedited footage and DVR storage media.
required_evidence: CCTV video footage covering the occurrence window and escape routes
Seizure memo of physical DVR/NVR hard drives (if live export is not possible)
Section 63 BSA electronic certificate signed by the CCTV system owner/operator
steps.condition_to_start: Mapping of surveillance cameras along the crime scene perimeter and approach routes.
steps.condition_to_complete: Procurement of relevant video footage accompanied by mandatory electronic admissibility certificates.
if_blocked: If private CCTV owners refuse cooperation or threaten to overwrite footage, execute an immediate search and seizure of the physical DVR instrument under BNSS Section 106.

steps.title: Firearm / Weapon Tracing & Licensing Verification
steps.description: If the homicide involved firearms, verify weapon serial numbers, caliber, and cartridge markings against the National Database on Arms and Licenses (NDAL-ALIS). Issue Section 94 BNSS notices to the Arms Licensing Authority to verify ownership, ammunition purchase ledgers, and dealer stock registers.
required_evidence: Arms license dossier and NDAL-ALIS UIN verification report
Ammunition purchase ledgers from licensed gunsmiths/dealers
FSL ballistic preliminary comparison report matching fired bullets/cartridges to suspect weapons
steps.condition_to_start: Autopsy or crime scene inspection confirms use of firearms or registered edged weapons.
steps.condition_to_complete: Weapon registration status verified and ownership trail established.
if_blocked: If the weapon is an unlicensed country-made firearm (Katta), interrogate informants and coordinate with State Crime Branch to trace the illicit manufacturing nexus.

steps.title: Search, Seizure of Weapon/Blood Clothes & Arrest of Accused
steps.description: Execute search warrants under BNSS Section 96 at suspect hideouts. Arrest the accused under BNSS Section 35. Conduct thorough interrogation leading to voluntary disclosure and discovery of hidden murder weapons or blood-stained clothes under Section 23 BSA (formerly Section 27 Evidence Act). Ensure mandatory medical examination of accused under BNSS Section 51/53.
required_evidence: Arrest memo and personal search memo of the accused
Voluntary disclosure memorandum recorded in the presence of independent witnesses
Seizure memo of recovered murder weapon and blood-stained garments recovered pursuant to disclosure
Medico-legal examination report and DNA profiling sample collection of accused u/s 51/53 BNSS
steps.condition_to_start: Actionable intelligence and evidentiary linkage established against suspect.
steps.condition_to_complete: Accused arrested, disclosure recorded, weapon/clothes recovered, and medical examination completed.
if_blocked: If the accused absconds across state boundaries, obtain a non-bailable warrant (NBW) from court and coordinate interstate transit remand with railway/state police units.

steps.title: Recording of Witness Statements & Judicial Confessions
steps.description: Record detailed statements of material witnesses, eyewitnesses, and first responders under BNSS Section 180 (formerly Section 161 CrPC). For critical eyewitnesses or voluntary confessions by accused, sponsor applications before the Magistrate for audio-video recording of statements under BNSS Section 183 (formerly Section 164 CrPC).
required_evidence: Written Section 180 BNSS statements of eyewitnesses, circumstantial witnesses, and panchas
Certified copy of Section 183 BNSS judicial statement / confession recorded by Magistrate
Audio-visual recording media of the Section 183 proceedings
steps.condition_to_start: Witnesses identified and accused willing to make a voluntary judicial confession.
steps.condition_to_complete: All material witness statements recorded and certified judicial statements procured from Magistrate.
if_blocked: If eyewitnesses face intimidation, immediately invoke witness protection protocols and request the trial court for name redaction and in-camera deposition.

steps.title: Compilation of Scientific Reports & Final Charge-Sheet Filing
steps.description: Collect all definitive scientific expert reports from FSL (serology, DNA matching, ballistics, toxicology) admissible under BNSS Section 329. Assemble the comprehensive chargesheet (police report) under BNSS Section 193 (formerly Section 173 CrPC) and file it before the jurisdictional court within the statutory 90-day timeline.
required_evidence: Certified FSL reports confirming DNA matching between deceased's blood and stains on accused's weapon/clothes
Complete chain of custody registers (Malkhana registers and Road Certificates)
Final chargesheet under BNSS Section 193 listing all accused, charges, witnesses, and exhibits
steps.condition_to_start: All investigative steps executed, accused remanded, and FSL forensic reports received.
steps.condition_to_complete: Formal submission and judicial cognizance of the final chargesheet before the Sessions/Magistrate Court.
if_blocked: If FSL reports are delayed near the 90-day statutory limit, file the primary chargesheet with available evidence to prevent default bail, and file the FSL report later as a supplementary chargesheet under BNSS Section 193(9).

dead_end_strategies.condition: Blind murder case with no eyewitnesses, unidentified corpse, and no hits on CCTV or cellular tower dumps.
suggested_actions: Upload corpse photographs, dental charts, and biometric fingerprints to the NCRB CCTNS portal and UIDAI database (via High Court order under entity_id uidai_aadhaar) to establish identity.
Perform forensic facial reconstruction or isotope analysis on skeletal remains at CFSL to determine geographical origin and socioeconomic profile of the deceased.
Analyse recent missing person reports across adjoining districts and railway corridors under entity_id railway_police matching the deceased's physical description and clothing labels.

title: Standard Operating Procedure for Investigation of Attempt to Murder Cases
source: Synthesized from BPR&D Police Investigation Manual, BNSS 2023, and Medico-Legal Case (MLC) Guidelines

steps.title: FIR Registration & Emergency Medical Evacuation
steps.description: Register FIR under BNSS Section 173 upon receiving information of a violent assault with intent to cause death. The first priority of the IO is to ensure immediate emergency medical evacuation of the injured victim to the nearest hospital without waiting for legal formalities, while deploying a guard to secure the crime scene. Note: Local police station / first responder unit is not present in the registry, hence department_entity_id is set to null.
required_evidence: Copy of recorded FIR under BNS Section 109 (formerly IPC Section 307)
Emergency hospital admission record / police dispatch log
Initial rough crime scene boundary inspection note
steps.condition_to_start: Report of violent assault involving dangerous weapons or severe trauma with intent to kill.
steps.condition_to_complete: Victim admitted to emergency medical care and FIR formally registered.
if_blocked: If private hospitals hesitate to admit the victim, serve an immediate notice citing Supreme Court guidelines (Pt. Parmanand Katara) and BNSS provisions mandating compulsory emergency treatment.

steps.title: Medico-Legal Case (MLC) & Injury Severity Certification
steps.description: Issue a formal police requisition to the treating hospital / forensic medical officer to prepare a detailed Medico-Legal Case (MLC) report. Specifically request certification on whether the injuries are 'dangerous to life', the dimensions and nature of wounds (incised, lacerated, gunshot), and weapon compatibility.
required_evidence: Certified Medico-Legal Case (MLC) report detailing exact wound measurements and locations
Surgeon's expert opinion stating whether the injury was sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death
Sealed packages containing bullets/pellets surgically extracted from the victim's body, or blood-soaked clothes removed during triage
steps.condition_to_start: Victim admitted to medical emergency room.
steps.condition_to_complete: Receipt of formal MLC report and surgically removed evidentiary exhibits under medical seal.
if_blocked: If the victim requires immediate major surgery, collect external wound photographs and blood samples in the preoperative room before surgical intervention alters wounds.

steps.title: Recording of Dying Declaration / Judicial Statement of Victim
steps.description: If the victim's condition is critical, immediately requisition a Judicial or Executive Magistrate to record a Dying Declaration under Section 26 BSA (formerly Section 32 Evidence Act). Obtain prior medical fitness certification from the treating doctor. If the victim survives, this statement operates as a highly substantive judicial statement under BNSS Section 183.
required_evidence: Doctor's written certificate endorsing the victim's mental fitness to give a statement
Certified copy of the Dying Declaration / Section 183 BNSS statement recorded by the Magistrate
Audio-visual recording of the statement recording process (if feasible)
steps.condition_to_start: Medical officer confirms victim is conscious and fit to make a statement, but critical.
steps.condition_to_complete: Magistrate successfully records and seals the victim's statement.
if_blocked: If no Magistrate can reach the hospital in time due to extreme emergency, the IO must record the statement in the presence of two independent witnesses and the treating doctor.

steps.title: Crime Scene Inspection & Blood Stain Seizure
steps.description: Summon the scientific experts / FSL team under BNSS Section 176(3) to inspect the scene. Lift liquid blood samples, blood-stained earth, control earth, weapon sheaths, or ballistic casings. Ensure accurate mapping of the assailant's vantage point and victim's position.
required_evidence: Seizure memos for bloodstains, trace evidence, and weapons found at spot
Spot inspection sketch map and scene photographs
Forensic scene examination report
steps.condition_to_start: Crime scene barricaded and secured by police guard.
steps.condition_to_complete: Physical exhibits lifted, sealed, labeled, and forwarded to FSL.
if_blocked: If rain or weather threatens outdoor bloodstains, immediately cover the spot with waterproof protective domes until scientific lifting is completed.

steps.title: Weapon Seizure, Arms Verification & Ballistic Requisition
steps.description: If a firearm was used, query the Arms Licensing Authority database under Section 94 BNSS to check weapon registration and license validity. Forward seized firearms, fired cartridge cases, and bullets extracted from the victim's body to FSL for ballistic comparison.
required_evidence: Seizure memo of firearm / edged weapon
Arms Licensing Authority verification report (for licensed weapons)
FSL ballistic comparison report confirming weapon operability and bullet matching
steps.condition_to_start: Weapon recovered from scene, suspect, or surgical extraction.
steps.condition_to_complete: Weapon registration verified and ballistic exhibits forwarded to laboratory.
if_blocked: If the weapon was dumped in a water body, deploy specialized police divers or municipal disaster response teams to recover the instrument before corrosion occurs.

steps.title: CCTV Surveillance & Telecom CDR Tracing
steps.description: Requisition CCTV footage from private establishments, housing societies, or municipal cameras covering the assault location and escape routes under BNSS Section 94. Simultaneously issue notices to TSPs for CDRs and Cell ID locations of suspects and victim to establish presence and prior enmity.
required_evidence: CCTV video footage showing the execution of assault or assailant flight
Section 63 BSA electronic admissibility certificates for video media
Telecom CDRs and cell tower geolocation mapping reports
steps.condition_to_start: Assault location and suspect mobile identities identified.
steps.condition_to_complete: Video surveillance media and telecom tracking logs procured and certified.
if_blocked: If CCTV is hosted on cloud servers operated by non-telecom ISPs, route Section 94 notices through entity_id isp_non_telecom.

steps.title: Arrest of Accused, Custody Remand & Medical Profiling
steps.description: Arrest the assailant under BNSS Section 35. Conduct mandatory medical examination under BNSS Section 51 and collect DNA/blood samples under Section 53 to match against bloodstains found on the victim. Produce accused before Magistrate and seek police custody remand under BNSS Section 187 for weapon recovery.
required_evidence: Arrest memo, personal search memo, and medical inspection report of accused
Voluntary disclosure statement leading to recovery of weapon or blood-stained clothes
Magistrate's order granting police custody remand under Section 187 BNSS
steps.condition_to_start: Evidentiary linkage established against suspect via victim statement, CCTV, or CDR.
steps.condition_to_complete: Accused arrested, medically profiled, biological samples drawn, and police remand secured.
if_blocked: If the accused claims an alibi, immediately verify their cellular tower location and workplace attendance logs under Section 94 BNSS to confirm or disprove the claim.

steps.title: Expert Report Synthesis & Final Charge-Sheet Filing
steps.description: Collect FSL chemical, serological, and ballistic reports. Ensure the hospital MLC report explicitly states the injury was dangerous to life (essential to sustain BNS Section 109 / IPC 307 charge). Compile and file the final chargesheet under BNSS Section 193 before the competent court.
required_evidence: Final FSL serology/ballistic reports admissible under BNSS Section 329
Final MLC / Wound Certificate with explicit life-endangerment medical opinion
Comprehensive police chargesheet under BNSS Section 193 accompanied by all witness statements and exhibits
steps.condition_to_start: Investigation completed, accused remanded, and medical/forensic reports received.
steps.condition_to_complete: Charge-sheet formally filed and cognizance taken by the jurisdictional Magistrate/Sessions Court.
if_blocked: If the victim subsequently succumbs to injuries during investigation, immediately submit a memo to court altering the charge from Attempt to Murder (BNS 109) to Murder (BNS 103) and conduct inquest/autopsy.

dead_end_strategies.condition: Victim is comatose or suffering from severe amnesia, unable to identify assailants, and assault occurred in an unmonitored blind spot.
suggested_actions: Conduct a rigorous victim background profiling: examine financial disputes, recent property mutations under entity_id sub_registrar_property, or litigation history to identify motives.
Analyse the victim's Call Detail Records (CDR) for the 30 days preceding the assault to identify threats, frequent unknown callers, or sudden communication breaks.
Perform automated ANPR (Automatic Number Plate Recognition) analysis across regional transport checkpoints under entity_id rto_parivahan for vehicles leaving the vicinity at high speed post-incident.

crime_type: Culpable Homicide Not Amounting to Murder
title: Standard Operating Procedure for Investigation of Culpable Homicide Not Amounting to Murder
source: Synthesized from BPR&D Homicide Investigation Guidelines, BNSS 2023, and Indian Penal Jurisprudence (Exceptions to Murder)

steps.title: FIR Registration & Preliminary Legal Classification
steps.description: Register FIR under BNSS Section 173 for unlawful homicide. Evaluate initial facts to determine if the act falls under Culpable Homicide Not Amounting to Murder (BNS Section 105 / IPC Section 304) — such as death caused by sudden provocation, sudden fight without premeditation, exceeding right of private defense, or rash/negligent assault without intent to kill. Note: Local police station / first responder unit is not present in the registry, hence department_entity_id is set to null.
required_evidence: Copy of recorded FIR under BNS Section 105
Initial crime scene inspection memo noting absence of premeditation markers (e.g., improvised weapons found at spot)
First responder logbook entries
steps.condition_to_start: Receipt of information regarding a death resulting from sudden altercation, brawl, or reckless assault.
steps.condition_to_complete: FIR registered and preliminary classification between Murder (BNS 103) and Culpable Homicide (BNS 105) documented in case diary.
if_blocked: If intent is ambiguous, initially register the FIR under the higher charge of Murder (BNS Section 103) and subsequently alter the section upon evidence of sudden provocation or lack of premeditation.

steps.title: Inquest Proceedings & Medico-Legal Post-Mortem Autopsy
steps.description: Conduct inquest proceedings under BNSS Section 194. Forward the corpse for post-mortem autopsy with a specific questionnaire to the medical officer: determine exact cause of death, whether injuries were fatal in ordinary course of nature, force applied, and whether death resulted from a single blow or repeated premeditated trauma.
required_evidence: Inquest Report (Panchnama) with detailed external injury descriptions
Certified Medico-Legal Post-Mortem Autopsy Report
Surgeon's specific opinion regarding the force of impact and fatal nature of individual blows
steps.condition_to_start: Corpse secured at the crime scene or hospital.
steps.condition_to_complete: Autopsy finalized, medical opinion on injury lethality received, and biological samples preserved.
if_blocked: If the defense claims death occurred due to pre-existing medical conditions (e.g., enlarged spleen or cardiac arrest during a minor scuffle), request histopathological examination of organs at FSL.

steps.title: Crime Scene Examination & Spontaneous Weapon Seizure
steps.description: Summon the FSL scientific team under BNSS Section 176(3). Inspect the scene to document evidence of a sudden brawl or struggle (overturned furniture, scattered belongings). Seize weapons of opportunity (wooden logs, stones, domestic utensils, agricultural tools) used in the heat of passion.
required_evidence: Seizure memos for spontaneous weapons, bloodstains, and broken objects at the scene
Photographic and sketch map documentation of the altercation arena
FSL scientific scene inspection report
steps.condition_to_start: Crime scene secured by investigating police team.
steps.condition_to_complete: Physical exhibits lifted, sealed, labeled, and dispatched to laboratory.
if_blocked: If the incident occurred in a crowded establishment (bar, restaurant), immediately seize guest registers and order slips under Section 94 BNSS to identify all patrons present.

steps.title: Recording Statements to Verify Sudden Provocation / Fight
steps.description: Examine eyewitnesses and record statements under BNSS Section 180. Focus questioning on establishing the statutory exceptions: did the deceased offer grave and sudden provocation? Was there a sudden fight upon the heat of passion without premeditation? Did the accused take undue advantage or act in a cruel/unusual manner?
required_evidence: Section 180 BNSS statements of eyewitnesses detailing the exact sequence of verbal altercation leading to physical violence
Section 183 BNSS judicial statements recorded by Magistrate for independent neutral witnesses
Audio-video recordings of witness examinations (where applicable under BNSS)
steps.condition_to_start: Eyewitnesses or bystanders identified from the crime scene.
steps.condition_to_complete: Comprehensive witness testimony compiled establishing the lack of premeditation or presence of provocation.
if_blocked: If eyewitnesses give conflicting accounts regarding who initiated the aggression, re-examine the physical injury patterns on both deceased and accused to reconstruct the sequence.

steps.title: Arrest of Accused, Injury Documentation & Medical Examination
steps.description: Arrest the accused under BNSS Section 35. Conduct immediate medical examination under BNSS Section 51/53. Meticulously document any defensive wounds, bruises, or injuries on the accused's body, which serve as critical evidence of a mutual fight or scuffle.
required_evidence: Arrest memo and personal search memo
Accused Medico-Legal Examination Report detailing defense wounds or mutual struggle injuries
Seizure memo of accused's blood-stained clothing worn during the altercation
steps.condition_to_start: Suspect apprehended by investigating team.
steps.condition_to_complete: Accused arrested, injuries medically certified, and clothing seized under seal.
if_blocked: If the accused claims they acted in self-defense against a lethal attack by the deceased, collect medical records of any prior assaults or threats between the parties.

steps.title: CCTV Footage & Telecom Enmity Verification
steps.description: Requisition CCTV footage from private sources or municipal cameras covering the altercation spot under BNSS Section 94 to visually verify who initiated the fight. Requisition telecom CDRs to check whether the accused and deceased had prior communication, planning, or longstanding enmity.
required_evidence: CCTV footage showing the spontaneous initiation of the altercation and physical struggle
Section 63 BSA electronic admissibility certificates
Telecom CDR analysis report confirming or ruling out prior premeditated coordination
steps.condition_to_start: Surveillance cameras or mobile phones identified at the scene.
steps.condition_to_complete: Video and telecom evidence procured and evaluated for premeditation markers.
if_blocked: If private establishments refuse CCTV footage, execute an immediate seizure of the DVR/NVR under BNSS Section 106.

steps.title: Forensic Toxicology & Alcohol/Drug Screening Requisition
steps.description: Since culpable homicide brawls frequently involve intoxication, submit preserved blood and viscera samples of both deceased and accused to FSL under BNSS Section 329 for toxicological screening. Determine blood alcohol concentration (BAC) or presence of psychotropic drugs to establish state of intoxication during the fight.
required_evidence: Certified FSL Toxicological Report establishing BAC / drug levels in deceased and accused
FSL Serological report matching bloodstains on spontaneous weapons to the deceased
steps.condition_to_start: Biological samples of deceased and accused collected during autopsy/arrest.
steps.condition_to_complete: Receipt of formal chemical and toxicological analysis reports from FSL.
if_blocked: If the laboratory faces pendency, request expedited testing from the Director FSL citing statutory remand expiration timelines.

steps.title: Legal Synthesis & Final Charge-Sheet Filing
steps.description: Synthesize medical, forensic, and witness evidence to firmly establish that while the accused had knowledge or intention that the blow could cause death, the act occurred under statutory mitigating circumstances (sudden fight, provocation). File final chargesheet under BNSS Section 193 specifying BNS Section 105 (Part I or Part II based on intent vs. knowledge).
required_evidence: Comprehensive police chargesheet under BNSS Section 193
All FSL scientific reports, autopsy findings, and MLC certificates
Evaluative legal memorandum in case diary justifying charge under BNS 105 over BNS 103
steps.condition_to_start: Investigation completed, evidence compiled, and statutory reports received.
steps.condition_to_complete: Charge-sheet formally filed and cognizance taken by the jurisdictional court.
if_blocked: If the Magistrate disagrees with the lower classification and considers the act premeditated murder, be prepared to submit supplementary evidence supporting framing of charges under alternate heads (BNS 103 r/w 105).

dead_end_strategies.condition: Death occurred days after a minor road-rage or street altercation due to internal hemorrhage, with no CCTV footage and witnesses refusing to testify.
suggested_actions: Requisition emergency vehicle dispatch logs (108 ambulance) and initial hospital admission triage notes under Section 94 BNSS to record the victim's earliest spontaneous statements regarding the altercation.
Analyse e-Challan and toll plaza databases under entity_id rto_parivahan along the route of the road-rage incident to identify vehicle registration numbers and owners present at the exact timestamp.
Examine the weapon of opportunity (e.g., vehicle tire iron or helmet) for latent fingerprints or epithelial touch-DNA at FSL to link the physical object directly to the accused.

title: Standard Operating Procedure for Procedural Investigation of Rape and Sexual Assault Cases (Adult Victim)
source: Synthesized strictly from BPR&D SOP for Investigation and Prosecution of Rape Cases, BNSS 2023, and MHA Guidelines

steps.title: Mandatory FIR Registration by Woman Officer & Forthwith Magistrate Dispatch
steps.description: In accordance with BPR&D SOP and BNSS Section 173 (formerly CrPC Section 154), immediately register the FIR upon receipt of information. The FIR MUST be recorded by a woman police officer or any woman officer. The victim can lodge the FIR in any police station (Zero FIR principle), which shall subsequently be transferred to the jurisdictional station. A copy of the FIR shall be given forthwith, free of cost, to the victim. Under BNSS Section 175 (formerly CrPC Section 157), an unedited copy of the FIR MUST be dispatched forthwith to the jurisdictional Magistrate within 24 hours without fail. Note: Local police station is not present in the registry, hence department_entity_id is set to null.
required_evidence: Copy of recorded FIR signed by woman police officer with exact date and hour of recording [1.2.1]
Written acknowledgment of free FIR copy handover to the survivor
Official dispatch receipt proving delivery of FIR copy to the Magistrate within 24 hours
steps.condition_to_start: Survivor or informant approaches police station or transmits information regarding sexual assault.
steps.condition_to_complete: FIR registered by woman officer, free copy provided to survivor, and statutory dispatch to Magistrate completed within 24 hours.
if_blocked: If a woman police officer is not available at the station, the DCP/SP of the district must immediately depute a woman officer from another station or specialized unit to record the FIR [1.1.5].

steps.title: Emergency Medico-Legal Examination of Victim within 24 Hours
steps.description: Under BNSS Section 184 (formerly CrPC Section 164-A) and BPR&D SOP, the Investigating Officer (accompanied by a female police officer) MUST arrange for the medico-legal examination of the victim as soon as possible, and strictly within 24 hours from the time of receiving information, at the nearest government hospital. The examination shall be conducted strictly by a female registered medical practitioner. Mandatory informed written consent of the victim must be obtained prior to examination. The IO shall prepare an injury sheet detailing scratches, bruises, and nail marks to accompany the victim. The medical officer shall collect sexual assault evidence (vaginal/anal swabs, smear slides, clothing, blood samples) using standardized Sexual Assault Forensic Evidence (SAFE) kits.
required_evidence: Informed written consent form signed by the adult victim [1.1.5]
Police injury sheet prepared by IO accompanying the victim
Certified Medico-Legal Examination Report prepared by female medical officer u/s 184 BNSS
Sealed SAFE kit containing biological exhibits, clothing, and swabs with medical officer's specimen seal
steps.condition_to_start: FIR registered and victim available for medical examination.
steps.condition_to_complete: Medical examination finalized within 24 hours by female doctor and sealed SAFE kit handed over to police escort under seizure memo.
if_blocked: If the victim refuses medical examination, the woman IO must explain the evidentiary importance of forensic samples; if refusal persists, document the formal written refusal signed by the victim in the presence of an NGO/support person [1.1.5].

steps.title: Mandatory Judicial Statement Recording u/s 183 BNSS by Magistrate
steps.description: In compliance with BNSS Section 183 (formerly CrPC Section 164) and BPR&D SOP, the IO shall sponsor an application to the Chief Judicial Magistrate to record the statement of the victim at the earliest possible instance. The statement shall be recorded by a female Judicial Magistrate. The recording shall preferably be audio-videographed as permitted under BNSS Section 183. The IO must ensure no police presence inside the chamber during judicial recording.
required_evidence: Police application submitted to CJM requesting appointment of female Magistrate for statement recording
Certified sealed copy of the judicial statement recorded u/s 183 BNSS by the Magistrate [1.1.5]
Audio-video recording storage media (if utilized by the Magistrate)
steps.condition_to_start: Victim medically examined and medically/psychologically fit to depose.
steps.condition_to_complete: Judicial statement formally recorded by female Magistrate and sealed copy placed in court records.
if_blocked: If the victim is temporarily or permanently mentally or physically disabled, the Magistrate shall take the assistance of an interpreter or special educator and video record the statement u/s 183(5) BNSS [1.2.1].

steps.title: Crime Scene Protection, Videography & Evidentiary Seizure
steps.description: Under BPR&D SOP and BNSS Section 176(3), whoever arrives at the scene first must safeguard and rope off the area with crime scene tape. The scene MUST be carefully documented and videographed from all directions before lifting exhibits. The IO or FSL/CFSL team must systematically collect blood-stained clothing, bedsheets, soil, biological fluids, hair, and electronic evidence (CCTV footage) under Seizure Memos. A detailed spot map must be drawn depicting distances.
required_evidence: High-resolution videography and photographic log of the un-tampered crime scene [1.1.4]
Seizure memos for bedsheets, clothing, biological stains, and physical exhibits lifted from spot
Detailed Spot Map indicating distances between evidentiary objects
Section 63 BSA electronic admissibility certificate for any CCTV footage recovered
steps.condition_to_start: Identification of the specific indoor or outdoor crime scene location.
steps.condition_to_complete: Scene videographed, spot map drawn, and physical exhibits scientifically packaged to prevent contamination or putrefaction.
if_blocked: If the crime scene is a moving vehicle or public transport, immediately impound the vehicle under BNSS Section 106 and seal it in the police station malkhana until FSL inspection.

steps.title: Arrest of Accused & Mandatory Medical / DNA Examination
steps.description: Upon establishing identity, arrest the accused under BNSS Section 35. In strict compliance with BNSS Sections 51, 52, and 53 (formerly CrPC Sections 53/53A), forward the arrested accused immediately to a registered medical practitioner for comprehensive medical examination. The medical officer shall document age, marks of violence/resistance, take DNA profiling samples (blood, semen, hair, pubic hair, nail clippings), and certify whether the accused is capable of performing sexual intercourse.
required_evidence: Arrest memo and personal search memo of the accused
Certified Accused Medico-Legal Examination Report under BNSS Section 52/53 detailing potency and injury marks [1.1.4]
Sealed forensic kit containing accused's blood, hair, nail scrapings, and DNA profiling samples with doctor's seal
steps.condition_to_start: Accused apprehended by investigating team.
steps.condition_to_complete: Accused arrested, medical potency certification received, and sealed DNA/biological samples handed over to police.
if_blocked: If the accused refuses to allow blood/biological sample collection, the medical officer and IO are statutorily empowered under Section 52(2) BNSS to use such reasonable force as is necessary to collect the samples.

steps.title: Dispatch of Sealed Forensic Exhibits & DNA Profiling Requisition
steps.description: Assemble all sealed SAFE kits from the victim, medical kits from the accused, and physical exhibits from the crime scene. In accordance with BPR&D SOP and BNSS Section 329 (formerly CrPC Section 293), forward all sealed packages through a secure Road Certificate to the State FSL / CFSL without delay. Requisition specific serological matching, DNA profiling and comparative analysis between victim's samples, accused's samples, and scene exhibits.
required_evidence: Official forwarding letter addressed to Director FSL / CFSL detailing the questionnaire
Copy of Road Certificate (RC) and Malkhana register entry proving intact chain of custody
Specimen seal impression letter verifying seals on SAFE kits and exhibit packages
Certified FSL Serological and DNA Profiling Expert Report admissible u/s 329 BNSS
steps.condition_to_start: Sealed biological kits and scene exhibits gathered in station malkhana.
steps.condition_to_complete: Exhibits formally accepted by FSL and scientific DNA profiling analysis report delivered to IO.
if_blocked: If FSL intake is delayed due to backlog, the IO must obtain an expedited prioritization endorsement from the DCP/SP of the district citing statutory time limits [1.1.5].

steps.title: Mandatory Supervisory Monitoring & Special Report Dispatch
steps.description: In strict compliance with BPR&D SOP, as rape cases are Grave/Special Report Cases, the investigation MUST be actively monitored by the Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) / Superintendent of Police (SP) of the district concerned. An Initial Special Report giving details of facts, evidence available, and instructions to IOs shall be issued by a Gazetted Officer within 72 hours of occurrence. Continuation Special Reports shall be issued fortnightly regarding investigation progress.
required_evidence: Fortnightly Continuation Special Reports signed by DCP/SP logging investigative guidance
Supervisory inspection notes in the official Case Diary
steps.condition_to_start: Registration of FIR for sexual assault.
steps.condition_to_complete: Initial Special Report dispatched within 72 hours and continuous fortnightly monitoring logged until chargesheet filing.
if_blocked: If the woman IO faces administrative bottlenecks in securing forensic or medical coordination, the monitoring DCP/SP must immediately intervene using district executive authority [1.1.5].

steps.title: Mandatory Completion of Investigation & Charge-Sheet Filing within 60 Days
steps.description: In strict compliance with statutory mandate under BNSS Section 193(3) (formerly CrPC Section 173(1A)) and BPR&D SOP, the investigation of rape MUST be completed within 2 months (60 days) from the date on which information was recorded by the police. The IO shall compile the final chargesheet incorporating FIR, MLC reports, Section 183 BNSS judicial statement, FSL DNA report, and witness statements, and file it before the jurisdictional Special Court / Sessions Court.
required_evidence: Comprehensive Police Charge-Sheet under BNSS Section 193 filed within 60 days of FIR [1.2.2]
Complete list of witnesses and relied-upon evidentiary documents (MLC, FSL DNA report, Section 183 statement)
Formal judicial order taking cognizance of the charge-sheet by the Special / Sessions Court
steps.condition_to_start: All investigation steps, witness examinations, and forensic requisitions finalized.
steps.condition_to_complete: Charge-sheet formally submitted and accepted by the court strictly within the statutory 60-day window.
if_blocked: If the FSL DNA report is delayed beyond 50 days, file the primary chargesheet within 60 days with MLC and Section 183 statements to comply with BNSS Section 193(3), and submit the FSL report upon receipt as a supplementary chargesheet u/s 193(9) BNSS.

dead_end_strategies.condition: Assault occurred in a secluded, unmonitored outdoor area, accused is an unknown stranger, and victim is unable to provide a detailed facial description due to trauma or darkness.
suggested_actions: Deploy mobile forensic units to lift touch-DNA and biological fluids from the victim's clothing and body; upload the extracted DNA profile to state and national offender DNA databases for cold-hit matching.

Requisition cell tower dump logs from all surrounding cellular base stations under entity_id telecom_operator covering a 2-hour window around the incident; cross-reference active mobile numbers against records of history-sheeters and repeat sexual offenders u/s BNSS.

Utilize forensic psychologists and trained facial composites experts at state CID under entity_id state_cyber_cell_cid to conduct cognitive interviewing of the survivor once medically stabilized to reconstruct an accurate facial composite.

title: Standard Operating Procedure for Procedural Investigation of POCSO / Child Sexual Abuse Cases
source: Synthesized strictly from BPR&D SOP for POCSO Investigations, POCSO Act 2012, POCSO Rules 2020, and Model Guidelines u/s 39

steps.title: Mandatory FIR Registration u/s 19 POCSO Act & Child-Friendly Intake
steps.description: In strict compliance with Section 19 of the POCSO Act and BPR&D SOP, immediately register the FIR upon receiving information of an offense against a child. The FIR MUST be recorded by a woman police officer designated as Child Welfare Police Officer (CWPO) or an officer of the Special Juvenile Police Unit (SJPU). Under Section 24 POCSO Act, the police officer SHALL NOT be in uniform during recording or examination. Under Section 24(4), NO CHILD can be held or detained overnight in a police station for any reason whatsoever. The information shall be recorded in simple language understandable to the child. A copy of the FIR shall be provided forthwith, free of cost, to the child's parent/guardian. Note: Local police station / SJPU is not present in the registry, hence department_entity_id is set to null.
required_evidence: Copy of recorded FIR under POCSO Act read with relevant BNSS sections [1.2.2]
Logbook entry confirming recording by a woman police officer / CWPO not in uniform
Written acknowledgment of free FIR copy handover to parent/guardian
Dispatch receipt confirming sending of FIR copy to Special POCSO Court / Magistrate within 24 hours
steps.legal_basis: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act Section 19
steps.condition_to_start: Receipt of information from any person, caregiver, school, or medical facility regarding sexual offense against a minor.
steps.condition_to_complete: FIR registered in child-friendly manner without uniform, free copy provided, and child safely handed over to parent/guardian or shelter.
if_blocked: If the child's parent/guardian is implicated in the abuse (incest u/s 5(n) POCSO), immediately remove the child to a specialized shelter home and take consent/presence of a Child Welfare Committee member or NGO representative for FIR registration.

steps.title: Mandatory 24-Hour Notification to CWC & Support Person Appointment
steps.description: In strict compliance with Section 19(6) of the POCSO Act and Rule 4(7) of POCSO Rules, the CWPO / Investigating Officer MUST report the matter to the local Child Welfare Committee (CWC) within 24 hours of recording the FIR. Concurrently, the IO must request the CWC / District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) to appoint a trained Support Person to render assistance to the child throughout the process of investigation and trial, preventing secondary victimization.
required_evidence: Official statutory notification letter dispatched to the Child Welfare Committee (CWC) within 24 hours [1.2.4]
CWC order / acknowledgment confirming receipt of notification and initiation of Child Protection Plan (CPP)
Formal appointment order of the designated Support Person issued by CWC/DLSA
steps.legal_basis: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act Section 19(6)
steps.condition_to_start: FIR registered under POCSO Act.
steps.condition_to_complete: CWC notified within statutory 24-hour window and formal Support Person assigned to the child victim.
if_blocked: If the CWC is not sitting on a weekend/holiday, serve the mandatory statutory notification directly to the CWC Chairperson or Member at their residence via registered electronic/physical dispatch.

steps.title: Emergency Medical Examination u/s 27 POCSO Act within 24 Hours
steps.description: Under Section 27 of the POCSO Act read with BNSS Section 184 (formerly CrPC Section 164-A) and BPR&D SOP, the IO must ensure medical examination of the child within 24 hours of receiving information, at the nearest government hospital. Under Section 27(2), the examination SHALL be conducted in the presence of the parent of the child, or any other person in whom the child has trust and confidence (such as the Support Person). In case of a female child, the examination SHALL be conducted by a woman medical practitioner. Under statutory guidelines, the invasive two-finger test is strictly prohibited. The doctor shall collect biological evidence using child-SAFE kits.
required_evidence: Certified Medico-Legal Examination Report prepared by woman doctor u/s 27 POCSO r/w 184 BNSS
Sealed forensic SAFE kit containing biological exhibits and clothing with medical officer's seal
Medical verification confirming examination was conducted in the presence of trusted adult/parent u/s 27(2)
steps.legal_basis: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act Section 27
steps.condition_to_start: FIR registered and child available for medical examination.
steps.condition_to_complete: Medical examination completed within 24 hours by woman doctor in presence of trusted adult, and sealed SAFE kit handed over to police.
if_blocked: If the parent/guardian refuses medical examination out of social stigma, the CWPO and CWC Support Person must counsel them on statutory requirements; if refusal persists, obtain written refusal endorsed by CWC [1.2.4].

steps.title: Child-Friendly Police & Judicial Statement Recording u/s 24/25 POCSO Act
steps.description: Under Section 24 POCSO Act, the police statement of the child shall be recorded at the residence of the child or at a place where the child usually resides or at a place of choice of the child, by a woman police officer not in uniform. Under Section 24(3), the IO must ensure that the child is NEVER in any way brought in contact with the accused. Under Section 25 POCSO Act read with BNSS Section 183 (formerly CrPC Section 164), the IO shall sponsor an application to the Magistrate to record the judicial statement as soon as possible. Under Section 26 POCSO Act, the Magistrate SHALL record the statement as spoken by the child, preferably with the assistance of an interpreter/special educator if needed, and ensure audio-visual recording.
required_evidence: Certified copy of judicial statement recorded u/s 25 POCSO Act read with BNSS Section 183 by Magistrate
Audio-video electronic recording storage media of the statement recording
Statutory log confirming no contact occurred between child and accused during recording
steps.legal_basis: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act Section 24
steps.condition_to_start: Child medically examined and supported by CWC Support Person/parent.
steps.condition_to_complete: Police statement and Magistrate judicial statement formally recorded in child-friendly environment without uniform or accused contact.
if_blocked: If the child is traumatized and unable to speak before the Magistrate, request an adjournment and utilize child-friendly court rooms or video-conferencing with CWC support person assistance.

steps.title: Statutory Age Determination & Verification of Victim u/s 34 POCSO Act
steps.description: Under Section 34 of the POCSO Act read with Section 94 of the Juvenile Justice Act and BPR&D SOP, the IO must establish the exact age of the victim to confirm minor status (below 18 years). Issue Section 94 BNSS notices to obtain: (i) Birth certificate from the Municipal Corporation / Registrar of Births and Deaths; or (ii) Date of birth certificate from the school first attended (matriculation/equivalent certificate). In the absence of documentary proof, immediately requisition a government medical board for ossification / radiological age estimation.
required_evidence: Certified Municipal Birth Certificate from Registrar of Births and Deaths; OR
Certified school matriculation / first attendance admission register copy showing date of birth; OR
Medical Board Ossification Age Estimation Report admissible under JJ Act Section 94
steps.legal_basis: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act Section 34
steps.condition_to_start: FIR registered under POCSO Act requiring definitive statutory proof of minority.
steps.condition_to_complete: Statutory documentary proof of age or medical ossification report procured and filed in case diary.
if_blocked: If school records are suspected to be forged or manipulated, immediately prioritize municipal birth registry extraction or medical ossification board evaluation [1.2.3].

steps.title: Arrest of Accused, Custody & Medical/DNA Sample Collection
steps.description: Apprehend the accused under BNSS Section 35. Under BPR&D SOP and BNSS Sections 51, 52, and 53, immediately forward the accused for medico-legal examination. The medical officer shall document injury marks, potency, and draw mandatory DNA profiling samples (blood, semen, hair, nail clippings). Note: If the accused is also a minor (CICL - Child in Conflict with Law), arrest procedures must strictly follow Section 10/13 JJ Act (no handcuffs, plain clothes, production before Juvenile Justice Board within 24 hours).
required_evidence: Arrest memo and personal search memo (or Apprehension memo for juvenile accused)
Certified Accused Medico-Legal Examination Report detailing potency and injury marks [1.1.4]
Sealed forensic kit containing accused's blood, hair, and DNA profiling samples with doctor's seal
JJB production order (if accused is a minor under JJ Act)
steps.condition_to_start: Evidentiary linkage and identity of accused established.
steps.condition_to_complete: Accused arrested (or apprehended if minor), potency certified, and sealed DNA samples secured.
if_blocked: If an adult accused absconds, obtain non-bailable warrant from Special POCSO Court and initiate proclamation proceedings u/s 84 BNSS.

steps.title: Dispatch of Sealed Forensic Exhibits & DNA Profiling Requisition
steps.description: In strict compliance with BPR&D SOP and BNSS Section 329, forward all sealed child-SAFE kits, accused medical kits, and crime scene exhibits through a secure Road Certificate to the State FSL / CFSL without delay. Requisition serological matching and comparative DNA profiling between the child victim's samples, accused's samples, and physical scene exhibits. Ensure chain of custody registers are scrupulously maintained.
required_evidence: Official forwarding letter addressed to Director FSL / CFSL detailing the questionnaire
Copy of Road Certificate (RC) and Malkhana register entry proving intact chain of custody
Specimen seal impression letter verifying seals on SAFE kits and exhibit packages
Certified FSL Serological and DNA Profiling Expert Report admissible u/s 329 BNSS
steps.condition_to_start: Sealed biological kits from victim and accused gathered in station malkhana.
steps.condition_to_complete: Exhibits formally accepted by FSL and scientific DNA profiling analysis report delivered to IO.

steps.title: Mandatory Investigation Completion within 60 Days & In-Camera Trial Setup
steps.description: In strict compliance with statutory mandate under BNSS Section 193(3) (formerly CrPC Section 173(1A)), POCSO Act Section 35, and BPR&D SOP, the investigation of child sexual abuse MUST be completed within 2 months (60 days) from the date of FIR. Assemble the chargesheet incorporating FIR, statutory age proof, MLC reports, Section 25 POCSO judicial statement, FSL DNA report, and CWC protection records. File the chargesheet before the designated Special POCSO Court. Ensure statutory coordination for in-camera trial u/s 33 POCSO Act and interim victim compensation u/s 33(8) POCSO Act.
required_evidence: Comprehensive Police Charge-Sheet under BNSS Section 193 filed strictly within 60 days of FIR [1.2.2]
Complete list of relied-upon documents (Age certificate, MLC, FSL DNA report, Section 25 statement)
Judicial order taking cognizance by Special POCSO Court and initiating in-camera trial protocols
Application submitted to Special Court / Legal Services Authority for interim victim compensation u/s 33(8) POCSO Act
steps.condition_to_start: All investigative steps, witness examinations, and age/forensic verification finalized.
steps.condition_to_complete: Charge-sheet submitted and accepted by Special POCSO Court within statutory 60-day window, and trial protection protocols activated.
if_blocked: If the FSL DNA report is pending at the 55-day mark, file the primary chargesheet within 60 days with MLC, age proof, and Section 25 statements to comply with BNSS Section 193(3), and submit the FSL report upon receipt as a supplementary chargesheet u/s 193(9) BNSS.

dead_end_strategies.condition: Child victim is pre-verbal or suffering from severe intellectual disability, unable to narrate the incident u/s 24/25 POCSO Act, and no direct eyewitnesses exist.
suggested_actions: In accordance with Section 24(2) and Section 25(1) POCSO Act, immediately engage a qualified special educator, speech therapist, or child psychologist from the approved CWC/DLSA panel to communicate using non-verbal methods, anatomical dolls, or drawings under video recording.

Rely heavily on scientific and physical evidence: prioritize immediate FSL collection of touch-DNA from the child's body/clothing and thorough biological examination of the suspect's garments and living quarters u/s BNSS.

Requisition medical records of any physical trauma, genital inflammation, or sexually transmitted infections (STIs) from treating pediatricians under Section 94 BNSS to establish the factum of abuse independently of verbal deposition.

title: Standard Operating Procedure for Investigation of Kidnapping and Abduction of Adults
source: Synthesized from BPR&D Investigation Manual, BNSS 2023, and Police Anti-Human Trafficking / Missing Persons Guidelines

steps.title: FIR Registration & Immediate All-India Police Broadcast
steps.description: Upon receipt of reliable information regarding wrongful taking, confinement, or abduction of an adult, register FIR under BNSS Section 173 (BNS Section 137 / 138; formerly IPC Section 363/365). Immediately upload victim photographs, physical identifiers, and suspected vehicle details onto the national NCRB CCTNS portal and issue a statewide wireless flash / all-station police broadcast. Note: Local police station / district control room is not present in the registry, hence department_entity_id is set to null.
required_evidence: Copy of recorded FIR under BNS Section 137/138
NCRB CCTNS missing/abducted person registration acknowledgment
Copy of all-station police wireless broadcast / hue and cry notice
steps.condition_to_start: Report of involuntary disappearance, abduction, or forcible kidnapping of an adult.
steps.condition_to_complete: FIR registered, national CCTNS alert uploaded, and wireless broadcast transmitted.
if_blocked: If the jurisdiction of kidnapping is disputed between stations, immediately register a Zero FIR and initiate pursuit without wasting time on territorial arguments.

steps.title: Telecom CDR, Cell Site Analysis & Live Location Tracking
steps.description: Issue urgent emergency requisitions under BNSS Section 94 to Telecom Service Providers for Call Detail Records (CDRs), Subscriber Application Forms (CAF), IMEI tracking, and real-time Cell Site / Tower location tracking of the victim's mobile phone and known suspect numbers.
required_evidence: CAF and CDRs with Cell ID locations for victim and suspect mobile numbers
Real-time cell tower triangulation / live location tracking logs
Section 63 BSA electronic admissibility certificates from TSP nodal officers
steps.condition_to_start: Victim or suspect mobile phone numbers identified.
steps.condition_to_complete: Live geolocation monitoring established and historical CDR communication graphs compiled.
if_blocked: If the victim's phone is powered off, perform last-active cell tower analysis and obtain subscriber details of all numbers that communicated with the victim in the 48 hours prior to abduction.

steps.title: CCTV Surveillance & Highway Toll Plaza ANPR Tracing
steps.description: Map the abduction spot and suspected escape routes. Issue Section 94 BNSS notices to private CCTV owners, municipal smart-city control rooms, and toll plaza operators under entity_id rto_parivahan to procure video surveillance and Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) logs of escaping vehicles.
required_evidence: CCTV video footage capturing the abduction or getaway vehicle
Toll plaza ANPR transaction logs showing vehicle registration number, timestamp, and direction of flight
Section 63 BSA electronic certificates for visual and ANPR media
steps.condition_to_start: Abduction location and suspected getaway vehicle type/color identified.
steps.condition_to_complete: Getaway vehicle registration number identified and highway escape trajectory mapped.
if_blocked: If fake number plates are used on the getaway vehicle, utilize RTO VAHAN database to cross-reference engine/chassis numbers from toll plaza high-resolution CCTV captures.

steps.title: Public Transport, Railway & Ride-Hailing Passenger Verification
steps.description: If the victim was abducted via public transport, taxis, or trains, issue Section 94 BNSS notices to railway police (GRP/RPF) for station CCTV and reservation charts, and to ride-hailing aggregators (Uber, Ola) for trip GPS telemetry, driver KYC, and booking logs.
required_evidence: Railway station CCTV footage and IRCTC / CRIS passenger reservation charts
Ride-hailing app trip GPS telemetry logs, driver KYC, and vehicle registration details
Written statements of transit staff, drivers, or co-passengers
steps.condition_to_start: Intelligence indicates victim was transported via trains, buses, or app-based cabs.
steps.condition_to_complete: Transit vehicle identified, driver/operator interrogated, and drop-off coordinates confirmed.
if_blocked: If cab bookings were made using burner phones, trace the payment method (UPI/card) through payment aggregators to identify the booking account holder.

steps.title: Border Checkpoint Alert & Look Out Circular (LOC) Issuance
steps.description: If intelligence suggests the victim is being abducted across international borders (e.g., Nepal, Bangladesh) or escaping via airports/seaports, immediately submit a formal proposal from SP/DCP rank to the Bureau of Immigration to open an emergency Look Out Circular (LOC) against the abductors.
required_evidence: MHA mandatory Proforma for opening Look Out Circular (LOC) signed by SP/DCP
Bureau of Immigration confirmation of LOC activation across airports and Integrated Check Posts (ICPs)
Passenger manifest and border crossing logs (if applicable)
steps.condition_to_start: Imminence of cross-border flight or international human smuggling established.
steps.condition_to_complete: LOC active across all immigration checkpoints and border security units alerted.
if_blocked: For open land borders (e.g., Indo-Nepal border), immediately coordinate with Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) border outposts to conduct physical vehicle inspections.

steps.title: Tactical Search, Hostage Rescue & Arrest of Abductors
steps.description: Execute tactical search and rescue operations under BNSS Section 96 at the identified hideout (derived from live CDR triangulation, ANPR tracking, or transit logs). Secure the safe recovery of the abducted victim. Arrest the kidnappers under BNSS Section 35 and seize weapons, vehicles, and communication gear.
required_evidence: Victim Recovery / Rescue Memorandum recorded in the presence of independent witnesses
Arrest memo, personal search memo, and medical inspection report of abductors
Seizure memo of getaway vehicles, weapons, ropes/ligatures, and mobile phones utilized in captivity
steps.condition_to_start: Actionable physical hideout location established via intelligence or technical tracking.
steps.condition_to_complete: Victim safely rescued, abductors arrested, and physical/digital exhibits seized.
if_blocked: If the hideout is in a fortified or hostile interstate terrain, coordinate with State Crime Branch / SWAT units before launching physical assault.

steps.title: Victim Medico-Legal Examination & Judicial Statement u/s 183 BNSS
steps.description: Immediately forward the rescued victim for medical examination under BNSS Section 184 to document physical injuries, sedation, or sexual assault. Sponsor an application before the Magistrate to record the victim's independent judicial statement under BNSS Section 183 (formerly Section 164 CrPC).
required_evidence: Certified Medico-Legal Case (MLC) report of the rescued victim detailing physical injuries or toxicology
Certified copy of Section 183 BNSS judicial statement recorded by the Magistrate
Audio-visual recording media of the judicial statement recording
steps.condition_to_start: Victim rescued and brought to safety.
steps.condition_to_complete: Medical examination finalized and independent judicial statement recorded by Magistrate.
if_blocked: If the victim is heavily sedated or suffering from Stockholm syndrome/trauma, provide psychological counseling at One Stop Centre before scheduling magisterial deposition.

steps.title: Evidence Synthesis & Final Charge-Sheet Filing
steps.description: Synthesize CDR tracking graphs, ANPR highway logs, rescue memos, FSL reports on seized weapons/sedatives, MLC reports, and Section 183 BNSS statements. Assemble and file the final chargesheet under BNSS Section 193 before the competent court within statutory timelines.
required_evidence: Comprehensive police chargesheet under BNSS Section 193 specifying BNS Sections 137/138 (or higher aggravated sections)
All FSL chemical/ballistic reports, ANPR electronic certificates, and telecom cell-site maps
Judicial cognizance order from the trial court
steps.condition_to_start: Investigation completed, abductors remanded, and scientific reports procured.
steps.condition_to_complete: Charge-sheet formally submitted and accepted by the jurisdictional court.
if_blocked: If the abduction was motivated by inter-caste marriage opposition (honor crime), immediately move the court for long-term police protection orders for the rescued couple.

dead_end_strategies.condition: Victim disappeared without witnesses, mobile phone was destroyed immediately at the abduction spot, and no ransom demands or extortion calls have been received.
suggested_actions: Conduct a deep victim financial and personal background investigation: query bank accounts and credit cards under entity_id bank_generic for sudden ATM withdrawals or digital transactions post-disappearance.

Check hospital emergency admission logs, unidentified accident victims, and mortuary registries across municipal jurisdictions under entity_id municipal_corporation to rule out hit-and-run accidents or medical emergencies.

Analyse the victim's social media and dating platform accounts under entity_id dating_matrimonial_platforms via Section 94 BNSS notices to check for catfishing, luring, or secret meetings arranged prior to disappearance.

title: Standard Operating Procedure for Investigation of Kidnapping for Ransom Cases
source: Synthesized from BPR&D Investigation Manual, BNSS 2023, and Special Cell / Crime Branch Kidnapping Negotiation SOPs

steps.title: FIR Registration & Covert Crisis Negotiation Setup
steps.description: Register FIR immediately under BNSS Section 173 (BNS Section 140; formerly IPC Section 364A). To protect hostage life, maintain strict media secrecy. Set up a covert police operational command desk at the victim family's residence. Install voice recording equipment and line-tap monitors on family telephones with statutory authorization. Note: Local police station / specialized anti-extortion cell is not present in the registry, hence department_entity_id is set to null.
required_evidence: Copy of recorded FIR under BNS Section 140 (Kidnapping for ransom)
Statutory interception / recording authorization order from competent authority
Initial crisis management logbook establishing communication protocols with family
steps.condition_to_start: Receipt of report regarding abduction accompanied by demands for ransom, extortion, or political concessions.
steps.condition_to_complete: FIR registered, covert command desk operational, and recording devices installed on family communication lines.
if_blocked: If the family is terrified and uncooperative with police presence out of fear of kidnapper retaliation, deploy plainclothes negotiators in unmarked vehicles to maintain covert liaison.

steps.title: Ransom Call Interception, VoIP Tracing & CDR Analysis
steps.description: Intercept and record all incoming ransom calls or text messages. Issue urgent notices under BNSS Section 94 to TSPs for real-time live location tracking, Cell ID tower dumps, and CDRs of caller numbers. If calls use internet VoIP (WhatsApp, Skype, FaceTime), serve notices on messaging intermediaries and ISPs to trace source IP addresses and SIP trunking gateways.
required_evidence: High-fidelity audio recordings of ransom calls and screenshots of extortion chats
Real-time cell tower triangulation and live location tracking logs of kidnapper phones
IPDR logs and subscriber KYC resolving VoIP public IP addresses to physical locations
Section 63 BSA electronic admissibility certificates
steps.condition_to_start: Kidnappers initiate communication demanding ransom via cellular call, SMS, or VoIP app.
steps.condition_to_complete: Ransom calls successfully intercepted, recorded, and technical geolocation tracing active.
if_blocked: If kidnappers use international spoofed numbers or burner SIMs active only for seconds, perform IMEI clustering to identify other SIM cards used in the same physical handset.

steps.title: Financial Surveillance of Bank Accounts, UPI VPAs & Crypto Wallets
steps.description: If kidnappers demand ransom payment via bank transfers, UPI VPAs, digital wallets, or cryptocurrency (Bitcoin/USDT), issue immediate notices under BNSS Section 106/94 to banks, NPCI, and Virtual Asset Service Providers (VASPs). Monitor accounts for withdrawal attempts, freeze balances upon deposit, and trace P2P crypto cash-out mules.
required_evidence: Bank statements, KYC dossiers, and IP login logs of designated ransom recipient bank accounts
VASP user KYC, wallet deposit ledgers, and blockchain transaction hash (TxID) tracking reports
BNSS Section 106 freezing order confirmations from banks and crypto exchanges
steps.condition_to_start: Kidnappers provide bank account numbers, UPI VPAs, or crypto wallet addresses for ransom payment.
steps.condition_to_complete: Financial tracking channels actively monitored, accounts frozen, and account holder identities extracted.
if_blocked: If crypto demands utilize decentralized privacy mixers, maintain automated blockchain monitoring while focusing tactical operations on cellular and physical drop-site leads.

steps.title: CCTV & Highway ANPR Surveillance of Abduction & Movement Routes
steps.description: Map the abduction spot and suspected movement corridors. Issue Section 94 BNSS notices to private CCTV owners, municipal smart-city control rooms, and toll plaza operators under entity_id rto_parivahan to procure video surveillance and Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) logs of suspect vehicles.
required_evidence: CCTV video footage capturing the abduction or vehicle movement along transit corridors
Toll plaza ANPR transaction logs showing vehicle registration, timestamp, and direction of travel
Section 63 BSA electronic admissibility certificates for visual and ANPR media
steps.condition_to_start: Abduction location and suspected getaway vehicle type/color identified.
steps.condition_to_complete: Getaway vehicle registration identified and highway movement trajectory mapped.
if_blocked: If vehicle number plates are obscured, identify vehicle make/model distinctives (stickers, body damage) across regional toll plaza CCTV captures.

steps.title: Tactical Trap / Ransom Drop-Site Surveillance & Hostage Rescue
steps.description: When kidnappers designate a physical drop-site for cash ransom, organize a covert tactical trap under BNSS Section 96. Use marked currency notes (treated with phenolphthalein powder or invisible UV ink if appropriate). Deploy plainclothes SWAT/crime branch teams around the drop zone. Prioritize hostage safety above immediate arrest: execute rescue raid simultaneously with or immediately following ransom handover.
required_evidence: Pre-trap memorandum listing serial numbers of currency notes and chemical treatment details
Hostage Recovery / Rescue Memorandum recorded at the spot in presence of independent witnesses
Post-trap recovery memorandum of marked ransom currency from apprehended kidnappers
High-resolution covert video/photographic recording of the ransom handover and tactical raid
steps.condition_to_start: Kidnappers finalize physical cash drop location and time with negotiating family.
steps.condition_to_complete: Hostage safely rescued, ransom retrieval operatives apprehended, and marked currency recovered.
if_blocked: If kidnappers change drop-sites repeatedly while moving in traffic, utilize aerial drone surveillance and GPS trackers concealed inside the ransom bag to maintain visual contact without compromising cover.

steps.title: Arrest of Syndicate, Voice Sample Seizure & Ballistic Recovery
steps.description: Arrest all gang operatives, negotiators, and hideout guards under BNSS Section 35. Seize weapons, vehicles, mobile phones, and captivity chains under Section 106/96 BNSS. Sponsor an application before the Magistrate under BNSS Section 349 (formerly Section 311A CrPC) to compel arrested accused to provide voice samples for spectrographic comparison against recorded ransom calls at FSL.
required_evidence: Arrest memos, personal search memos, and medical examination reports of all syndicate members
Seizure memos of weapons, getaway vehicles, mobile phones, and marked currency notes
Magistrate's order u/s 349 BNSS directing accused to provide voice samples
FSL Voice Spectrographic Comparison Report matching accused voice to recorded ransom calls
steps.condition_to_start: Hostage rescued and abductors apprehended.
steps.condition_to_complete: Syndicate arrested, weapons/phones seized, and voice samples extracted and matched by FSL.
if_blocked: If an accused refuses to provide voice samples despite court order u/s 349 BNSS, request the court to draw an adverse legal presumption under Section 119 BSA (formerly Section 114 Evidence Act).

steps.title: Victim Medico-Legal Examination & Judicial Statement u/s 183 BNSS
steps.description: Forward the rescued hostage immediately to a hospital under BNSS Section 184 for comprehensive Medico-Legal Case (MLC) examination to document physical torture, binding marks, malnutrition, or sedation. Requisition the Magistrate to record the victim's independent judicial statement under BNSS Section 183 detailing captivity conditions and identifying captors.
required_evidence: Certified Medico-Legal Case (MLC) report detailing captivity injuries, ligature marks, or toxicology
Certified copy of Section 183 BNSS judicial statement recorded by the Magistrate
Audio-visual recording media of the judicial statement recording
steps.condition_to_start: Hostage safely rescued from captivity.
steps.condition_to_complete: MLC examination finalized and independent judicial statement recorded by Magistrate.
if_blocked: If the victim suffers from extreme trauma or amnesia regarding hideout locations, conduct a supervised Test Identification Parade (TIP) of the hideout and accused under Section 54 BNSS once recovered.

steps.title: Evidence Synthesis & Final Charge-Sheet Filing
steps.description: Synthesize ransom call recordings, FSL voice spectrography reports, marked currency recovery memos, CDR live-tracking graphs, MLC reports, and Section 183 BNSS statements. Assemble and file the final chargesheet under BNSS Section 193 before the competent court invoking BNS Section 140 (carrying death penalty / life imprisonment).
required_evidence: Comprehensive police chargesheet under BNSS Section 193 specifying BNS Section 140
All FSL reports (voice spectrography, chemical note analysis, ballistics), ANPR logs, and CDR maps
Section 63 BSA electronic admissibility certificates for all audio recordings and digital tracks
Formal judicial order taking cognizance of the charge-sheet by the Sessions Court
steps.condition_to_start: All investigative steps executed, syndicate remanded, and FSL expert reports received.
steps.condition_to_complete: Charge-sheet formally submitted and accepted by the Sessions Court within statutory timelines.
if_blocked: If FSL voice spectrography reports face administrative delay near the statutory 90-day limit, file the primary chargesheet with CDRs and marked currency recovery memos, and file the voice report later u/s 193(9) BNSS.

dead_end_strategies.condition: Ransom negotiations are conducted entirely by an overseas syndicate via end-to-end encrypted darkweb chat rooms, hostage is held in an unknown domestic location by cut-out mercenaries, and no physical drop-site is used (pure crypto demand).
suggested_actions: Deploy advanced blockchain forensic tracking under entity_id vasp_crypto_exchange to monitor the ransom crypto wallet; identify exchange deposit off-ramps or P2P cash-out traders in India to trace the domestic financial beneficiaries.

Analyse pattern of life and proof-of-life media sent by kidnappers (photos/videos of hostage): examine background audio, lighting, architectural details, and electrical frequency humming (ENF analysis at FSL) to narrow down the geographic hideout location.

Conduct comprehensive intelligence screening of the victim's business associates, recently fired employees, and domestic staff to identify the local 'spotter' who provided the offshore syndicate with the victim's schedule and financial profile.

title: Standard Operating Procedure for Investigation of Human Trafficking and Commercial Sexual Exploitation
source: Synthesized strictly from BPR&D SOP on Investigation of Human Trafficking, ITPA 1956, and MHA Advisories

steps.title: FIR Registration & Pre-Rescue Intelligence Gathering
steps.description: Upon receipt of information regarding trafficking of women or children for commercial sexual exploitation, forced labor, or organ harvesting, register FIR under BNSS Section 173 (BNS Section 143; formerly IPC Section 370) read with relevant sections of the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956 (ITPA) and POCSO Act. Conduct discrete pre-rescue intelligence gathering under ITPA Section 13/15: verify brothel/workplace locations, identify traffickers/pimps, and map entry/exit points without alerting suspects. Note: Local police station / Anti-Human Trafficking Unit (AHTU) is not present in the registry, hence department_entity_id is set to null.
required_evidence: Copy of recorded FIR under BNS Section 143 read with ITPA Sections 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 [1.2.3]
Pre-rescue intelligence reconnaissance report and spot surveillance logs
List of identified traffickers, brothel keepers, and commercial facilitators
steps.condition_to_start: Receipt of intelligence, missing person link, or victim rescue call regarding human trafficking.
steps.condition_to_complete: FIR registered, target premises verified, and tactical rescue plan finalized by Special Police Officer (SPO).
if_blocked: If local police station personnel are suspected of collusion with brothel keepers, the raid and investigation must be directly executed by the district Anti-Human Trafficking Unit (AHTU) or State Crime Branch [1.1.3].

steps.title: Coordinated Tactical Search & Rescue Operation u/s 15 ITPA
steps.description: Under Section 15 of the ITPA read with BNSS Section 96, a designated Special Police Officer (SPO) / AHTU team shall execute a tactical search and rescue raid without prior warrant if delay would defeat the rescue. The raid team MUST include woman police officers and should associate independent social workers / NGO representatives as witness observers. Secure all victims safely. Arrest brothel keepers, traffickers, pimps, and customers (prosecutable under ITPA/POCSO/BNS). Seize cash, registers, mobile phones, condoms, and customer identity documents under Seizure Memos.
required_evidence: Arrest memos of traffickers, brothel managers, pimps, and customers found on premises
Seizure memos for account ledgers, cash, mobile phones, customer IDs, and physical paraphernalia
Video and photographic recording of the rescue operation and premises layout
steps.condition_to_start: Actionable intelligence and operational readiness established by Special Police Officer.
steps.condition_to_complete: Victims safely rescued, traffickers/customers arrested, and physical/digital evidence seized.
if_blocked: If brothel owners utilize concealed underground vaults or secret rooms to hide victims during raids, deploy architectural structural scanners and FSL teams to breach false walls [1.2.3].

steps.title: Post-Rescue Victim Care, Shelter Referral & CWC Notification
