steps.description: In strict compliance with ITPA Sections 16/17, POCSO Act, and BPR&D SOP, treat rescued victims with dignity as victims of crime, NOT offenders. Immediately separate victims from traffickers/employers. For minor victims, send mandatory notification to the Child Welfare Committee (CWC) within 24 hours under JJ Act Section 31 and transfer them to an approved Protective Rehabilitation Shelter Home. For adult female victims, refer to One Stop Centre or Protective Home u/s 17 ITPA.
required_evidence: Protective Shelter Home admission / handover custody acknowledgment receipts
Initial counselor trauma assessment report from One Stop Centre / Shelter
steps.condition_to_start: Victims extracted from exploitation premises during tactical raid.
steps.condition_to_complete: All victims safely housed in protective shelter homes and CWC statutorily notified within 24 hours.
if_blocked: If traffickers attempt to present fraudulent guardianship papers to claim custody of minor victims at the police station, strictly refuse handover and refer all custody adjudication exclusively to the CWC [1.2.3].

steps.title: Medico-Legal Examination & Statutory Age Determination
steps.description: Forward rescued victims for medico-legal examination under BNSS Section 184 (or POCSO Section 27 for minors) within 24 hours to document sexual violence, physical abuse, sexually transmitted infections, or malnutrition. Requisition statutory age verification: obtain municipal birth certificates or school records under Section 94 BNSS. In the absence of documents, refer victims to a government medical board for ossification / radiological age estimation under Section 94 JJ Act / Section 15 ITPA.
required_evidence: Municipal Birth Certificate or School Admission Register copy confirming date of birth; OR
Medical Board Ossification Age Estimation Report admissible under JJ Act / ITPA
steps.condition_to_start: Victims admitted to protective shelter care.
steps.condition_to_complete: Medical examination completed, injury/health profile documented, and statutory age legally established.
if_blocked: If medical age estimation yields a margin of error spanning across 18 years (e.g., 17-19 years), statutory jurisprudence mandates adopting the lower age to extend POCSO and juvenile protections to the victim [1.2.3].

steps.title: Recording of Judicial Statements u/s 183 BNSS by Magistrate
steps.description: Sponsor applications before the Chief Judicial Magistrate to record the independent judicial statements of all rescued victims under BNSS Section 183 (formerly Section 164 CrPC) at the earliest instance. For minor victims, statement recording must strictly adhere to Section 25 POCSO Act (child-friendly environment, female Magistrate, no uniform, audio-video recording). Ensure statements capture recruitment luring, transportation routes, financial bondage, and identification of traffickers/customers.
required_evidence: Police application submitted to CJM for statement recording under BNSS Section 183 / POCSO Section 25
Certified sealed copies of judicial statements recorded by the Magistrate
Audio-video recording media of the deposition proceedings
steps.condition_to_start: Victims medically examined and psychologically stabilized in shelter care.
steps.condition_to_complete: Judicial statements formally recorded by Magistrate and placed in court records.
if_blocked: If victims suffer from severe trauma or language barriers (interstate/cross-border victims), the Magistrate must appoint a certified translator or special educator to assist during deposition [1.2.1].

steps.title: Telecom, Transit & Inter-State/Cross-Border Route Tracing
steps.description: Issue Section 94 BNSS notices to TSPs for CDRs, tower dumps, and IMEI clustering of mobile phones seized from traffickers, pimps, and brothel managers to map the organized trafficking network. Requisition passenger reservation charts and CCTV footage from railway authorities (GRP/RPF) and bus terminals to trace the transportation of victims from source villages to destination cities.
required_evidence: Telecom CDRs, cell site analysis, and IMEI clustering reports linking recruiters, transporters, and brothel owners [1.2.3]
Railway reservation charts, ticketing IP logs, and station CCTV footage confirming victim transportation
Section 63 BSA electronic admissibility certificates for telecom and transit records
steps.condition_to_start: Trafficker mobile phones seized and source villages identified from victim statements.
steps.condition_to_complete: Complete transit mapping from source to destination established with certified electronic records.
if_blocked: If victims were transported via trains across multiple railway zones, coordinate with railway police under entity_id railway_police to pull historical booking ledgers from CRIS/IRCTC.

steps.title: Financial Follow-the-Money Tracing & Property Attachment
steps.description: Trafficking is an organized crime for commercial gain. Issue Section 94/106 BNSS notices to banks, UPI PSPs, and money transfer agents to freeze bank accounts, lockers, and digital wallets of brothel owners, traffickers, and syndicates. Query sub-registrar offices to identify real estate purchased with trafficking proceeds. Sponsor applications under BNSS Section 107 / Section 18 ITPA for attachment and closure of brothel premises and forfeiture of proceeds of crime.
required_evidence: Certified bank ledger statements and KYC dossiers of trafficking syndicate accounts [1.2.3]
BNSS Section 106 freezing orders for bank accounts and financial assets
Property title deeds and Encumbrance Certificates of brothel premises and syndicate real estate
Judicial attachment order under BNSS Section 107 / ITPA Section 18 ordering eviction and closure of brothel premises
steps.condition_to_start: Financial ledgers, bank books, or account numbers seized during rescue raid.
steps.condition_to_complete: Syndicate bank accounts frozen, real estate identified, and judicial property attachment orders procured.
if_blocked: If massive multi-state money laundering is uncovered, immediately refer the financial dossier to the Enforcement Directorate (ED) for parallel attachment under PMLA provisions.

steps.title: Comprehensive Charge-Sheet & Victim Rehabilitation Filing
steps.description: Compile the final chargesheet under BNSS Section 193 invoking BNS Section 143 (Trafficking), ITPA Sections 3-7, and POCSO Sections (for minors) against recruiters, transporters, brothel keepers, financiers, and exploitative customers. File the chargesheet before the Special Sessions Court within statutory timelines. Simultaneously move applications under Section 357A CrPC / BNSS Section 395 and victim compensation schemes for interim rehabilitation awards for rescued survivors.
required_evidence: All relied-upon documents: Rescue panchnama, MLCs, Age reports, Section 183 statements, CDR graphs, and financial freeze orders
Formal judicial order taking cognizance by the Special Court / Sessions Court
Application filed before District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) for victim compensation and rehabilitation awards
steps.condition_to_start: All investigative steps executed, syndicate remanded, and statutory reports received.
steps.condition_to_complete: Charge-sheet formally submitted and accepted by the court, and victim compensation proceedings initiated.
if_blocked: If cross-border traffickers (e.g., from Nepal or Bangladesh) reside outside India, coordinate with Interpol via CBI Nodal Officer to issue Red Notices and initiate extradition proceedings.

dead_end_strategies.condition: Rescued victims turn hostile during investigation due to severe trauma, debt-bondage threats against their rural families by source-village recruiters, or fear of social stigma.
suggested_actions: Build an independent, victim-less prosecution case relying on objective electronic and physical evidence: brothel account ledgers showing victim names/earnings, seized condoms, customer registers, CDR communication graphs, and rescue panchnamas.

Immediately invoke Witness Protection Schemes: arrange secure residential shelter relocation outside the victim's home state and request the court for in-camera trials with identity masking u/s BNSS/POCSO.
Coordinate with district police authorities in the victim's native source village to deploy protective patrols around the victim's family and arrest local debt-bondage recruiters threatening them.

title: Standard Operating Procedure for Investigation of Acid Attack and Corrosive Substance Assault Cases
source: Synthesized from BPR&D Investigation Guidelines, BNSS 2023, MHA Advisories, and Supreme Court Guidelines (Laxmi v. UOI / Parivartan Kendra)

steps.title: Immediate FIR Registration & Emergency Medical Evacuation / Free Treatment Requisition
steps.description: Upon receipt of information regarding an acid or corrosive substance attack, immediately register FIR under BNSS Section 173 (BNS Section 124; formerly IPC Section 326A/326B). The paramount duty of the IO is immediate medical evacuation of the victim to a specialized burn unit / hospital. In accordance with BNSS Section 396 (formerly CrPC Section 357C) and Supreme Court directives (Laxmi v. UOI), serve binding statutory notice on the hospital mandating immediate, free-of-cost first aid and medical treatment without waiting for legal formalities. Note: Local police station / first responder unit is not present in the registry, hence department_entity_id is set to null.
required_evidence: Copy of recorded FIR under BNS Section 124 (carrying minimum 10 years to life imprisonment)
Statutory notice served on hospital u/s 396 BNSS mandating free emergency medical treatment
Hospital admission and emergency triage log
steps.condition_to_start: Report of throwing or administering acid or chemical corrosive substance on any person.
steps.condition_to_complete: Victim admitted to specialized burn emergency care, free treatment initiated, and FIR formally registered.
if_blocked: If a private hospital demands monetary deposit or refuses admission, immediately initiate criminal prosecution against the hospital doctor/management under BNS Section 114 (formerly IPC Section 166B).

steps.title: Medico-Legal Case (MLC) & Chemical Burn Severity Certification
steps.description: Requisition the treating burn surgeon / forensic medical officer to prepare a comprehensive Medico-Legal Case (MLC) report. Specifically document the percentage and depth of chemical burns, permanent disfigurement, loss of vision/hearing, and bodily disability. Ensure the medical officer preserves chemical-soaked clothing, skin scrapings, and liquid acid washings from the victim's body in clean glass/polypropylene containers sealed with glass stoppers for FSL analysis.
required_evidence: Certified Medico-Legal Case (MLC) wound certificate detailing burn depth, disfigurement, and organ damage
Ophthalmological / specialized evaluation reports documenting visual or functional impairment
Sealed, non-reactive glass/plastic containers containing acid-soaked garments, skin debris, and chemical washings with doctor's specimen seal
steps.condition_to_start: Victim admitted to hospital burn unit.
steps.condition_to_complete: Receipt of detailed MLC report and sealed chemical burn exhibits from medical officer.
if_blocked: If the victim is undergoing emergency debridement surgery, ensure the forensic medical team collects external swab samples and burn photographs in the operating theater prior to wound dressing.

steps.title: Recording of Dying Declaration / Judicial Statement of Victim
steps.description: Due to high mortality and trauma in acid burn cases, immediately requisition a Judicial or Executive Magistrate to record the victim's statement / Dying Declaration under Section 26 BSA (formerly Section 32 Evidence Act) after obtaining medical fitness certification. If the victim survives, this statement operates as a substantive judicial deposition under BNSS Section 183. Ensure video recording of the statement.
required_evidence: Medical officer's written certification endorsing victim's mental fitness to give a statement
Certified copy of Dying Declaration / Section 183 BNSS judicial statement recorded by Magistrate
High-resolution audio-visual recording of the statement recording process
steps.condition_to_start: Treating surgeon certifies victim is conscious and mentally fit to depose.
steps.condition_to_complete: Magistrate formally records, videographs, and seals the victim's deposition.
if_blocked: If facial burns or endotracheal intubation prevent verbal speech, the Magistrate must record the statement via written notes, hand gestures, or communication boards under video recording.

steps.title: Forensic Crime Scene Examination & Corrosive Residue Seizure
steps.description: Summon the FSL chemical / forensic science team under BNSS Section 176(3). Inspect the attack location. Lift liquid chemical puddles using glass pipettes, collect acid-stained soil, control soil, melted objects, and containers/bottles discarded by the assailant. Package exhibits in airtight, chemical-resistant glass or virgin polypropylene containers to prevent reaction or evaporation.
required_evidence: Seizure memos for corrosive liquid residues, acid bottles, stained soil, and melted materials
High-resolution scene photographs and spot sketch map showing chemical splash patterns
FSL scientific scene examination report
steps.condition_to_start: Crime scene secured by investigating police team.
steps.condition_to_complete: All chemical and trace exhibits scientifically lifted, sealed in inert containers, labeled, and forwarded to FSL.
if_blocked: If rain or municipal washing threatens to dilute chemical residues on streets, immediately deploy pH test strips and lift surface swabs into distilled water vials before evidence is lost.

steps.title: Investigation of Acid / Corrosive Sale & Vendor Licensing Verification
steps.description: In compliance with Supreme Court guidelines (Laxmi v. UOI) and Model Poisons Rules regulating acid sales, investigate the source of the corrosive substance. Issue Section 94 BNSS notices to local chemical stockists, hardware vendors, and industrial suppliers. Requisition mandatory acid sale registers (recording buyer photo ID, address, and quantity). Verify vendor licensing compliance with the Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) / Excise authorities.
required_evidence: Certified extracts of mandatory Acid Sale Registers from chemical/hardware vendors
Vendor statutory retail license / permit verification report from SDM or Excise department
CCTV footage from retail chemical shops showing the buyer purchasing acid
Seizure memo of stock registers from non-compliant or illicit chemical vendors
steps.condition_to_start: Chemical identity of corrosive substance determined or general commercial acid used.
steps.condition_to_complete: Point of sale identified, vendor registers verified, and illegal chemical stockists prosecuted.
if_blocked: If the acid was stolen from an industrial workplace, educational laboratory, or battery repair shop, subpoena inventory ledgers and employee access logs of that establishment under Section 94 BNSS.

steps.title: CCTV Surveillance & Telecom Enmity Tracing
steps.description: Requisition CCTV footage from private establishments, housing societies, or municipal cameras covering the assault spot and escape routes under BNSS Section 94. Simultaneously issue notices to TSPs for CDRs and Cell ID locations of suspects and victim to establish presence, tracking, or prior harassment/stalking history.
required_evidence: CCTV video footage showing the execution of the acid attack or assailant flight
Section 63 BSA electronic admissibility certificates for video media
Telecom CDRs and cell tower geolocation mapping reports confirming suspect stalking/presence
steps.condition_to_start: Assault location and suspect mobile identities identified.
steps.condition_to_complete: Video surveillance media and telecom tracking logs procured and certified.
if_blocked: If CCTV is hosted on cloud servers operated by non-telecom ISPs, route Section 94 notices through entity_id isp_non_telecom.

steps.title: Arrest of Accused, Medical Chemical Profiling & Remand
steps.description: Arrest the assailant under BNSS Section 35. Conduct immediate medical examination under BNSS Section 51/53: specifically inspect and swab the accused's hands, face, and forearms for chemical burn marks or corrosive residues resulting from splash-back during the attack. Seize the accused's clothing worn during the incident under sealed glass containers.
required_evidence: Arrest memo, personal search memo, and medical inspection report of accused
Seizure memo of accused's clothing and chemical skin swabs sealed in inert containers
Voluntary disclosure statement leading to recovery of acid storage containers or weapons
Magistrate's order granting police custody remand under Section 187 BNSS
steps.condition_to_start: Evidentiary linkage established against suspect via victim statement, CCTV, or CDR.
steps.condition_to_complete: Accused arrested, chemically swabbed, clothing seized, and police remand secured.
if_blocked: If the accused claims an alibi, immediately verify cellular tower location and workplace attendance logs under Section 94 BNSS.

steps.title: FSL Chemical Report Synthesis, Compensation Award & Charge-Sheet Filing
steps.description: Procure definitive FSL Chemical Analysis reports under BNSS Section 329 confirming identical chemical composition (e.g., sulfuric acid, nitric acid) between liquid thrown on victim, residues at scene, stains on accused's clothes, and stock seized from vendor. File final chargesheet under BNSS Section 193 specifying BNS Section 124. Concurrently file formal application before District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) under BNSS Section 395 (formerly Section 357A CrPC) and NALSA Victim Compensation Scheme for mandatory statutory compensation award (minimum Rs. 3 Lakhs upwards) for rehabilitation and reconstructive surgeries.
required_evidence: Certified FSL Chemical Analysis Report matching corrosive substance across victim, scene, accused, and vendor exhibits
Comprehensive police chargesheet under BNSS Section 193 specifying BNS Section 124
All relied-upon documents: MLC, visual disability reports, Section 183 statements, CCTV, and vendor registers
Application filed before DLSA requesting immediate release of statutory victim compensation and surgical medical funding
steps.condition_to_start: Investigation completed, accused remanded, and FSL chemical reports received.
steps.condition_to_complete: Charge-sheet formally submitted and accepted by the Sessions Court, and statutory compensation proceedings initiated.
if_blocked: If DLSA compensation disbursement is delayed, move an urgent application before the trying Sessions Judge under BNSS Section 395(2) to pass an immediate interim compensation order against state funds.

dead_end_strategies.condition: Attack occurred at night in a blind spot by a masked, unidentified assailant on a two-wheeler without number plates, and the victim has no known enmity.
suggested_actions: Conduct exhaustive victim background profiling: examine rejected marriage proposals, workplace rivalries, or one-sided stalking history by analyzing mobile phone backup chat archives under Section 94 BNSS.
Perform chemical fingerprinting (trace impurity profiling) of the acid at CFSL to determine the specific industrial manufacturing batch and regional distributor network.

Analyse cell tower dump logs from all surrounding cellular base stations under entity_id telecom_operator covering the attack window; cross-reference active numbers against CDRs of individuals who frequently called or stalked the victim in the past year.

title: Standard Operating Procedure for Investigation of Grievous Hurt and Severe Assault Cases
source: Synthesized from BPR&D Police Investigation Manual, BNSS 2023, and Medico-Legal Jurisprudence (BNS Section 116/117)

steps.title: FIR Registration & Emergency Medical Evacuation
steps.description: Upon receipt of information regarding severe physical assault, register FIR under BNSS Section 173 (BNS Section 117/118; formerly IPC Section 325/326). Ensure immediate medical evacuation of the injured victim to the nearest hospital for emergency treatment, while dispatching a police team to safeguard the assault location. Note: Local police station / first responder unit is not present in the registry, hence department_entity_id is set to null.
required_evidence: Copy of recorded FIR under BNS Section 117/118
Emergency hospital admission record / police dispatch log
Initial rough spot boundary inspection note
steps.condition_to_start: Report of violent assault resulting in bone fractures, permanent impairment, or severe bodily trauma.
steps.condition_to_complete: Victim admitted to emergency medical care and FIR formally registered.
if_blocked: If the victim is unconscious, register the FIR on the statement of an eyewitness, relative, or the first responder police officer as state complainant.

steps.title: Medico-Legal Case (MLC) & Grievous Injury Certification
steps.description: Issue formal police requisition to the treating hospital / forensic medical officer for a detailed Medico-Legal Case (MLC) report. Specifically request certification on whether the injury falls under statutory definitions of 'Grievous Hurt' under BNS Section 116 (formerly IPC Section 320) — such as emasculation, permanent loss/impairment of sight, hearing, or joint, bone fracture/dislocation, facial disfigurement, or injury causing severe pain/inability to follow ordinary pursuits for 20 days.
required_evidence: Certified Medico-Legal Case (MLC) wound certificate detailing exact injury dimensions and locations
Radiological reports (X-ray, CT scan, MRI films) confirming bone fracture, dislocation, or internal organ trauma
Surgeon's definitive expert opinion classifying the injury as 'Grievous' under BNS Section 116
Sealed packages containing blood-soaked clothing removed from victim during medical triage
steps.condition_to_start: Victim admitted to hospital medical emergency.
steps.condition_to_complete: Receipt of formal MLC wound certificate, radiological proof of fracture/impairment, and sealed clothing exhibits.
if_blocked: If initial MLC marks injury as 'simple' pending X-ray, ensure follow-up requisition after 20 days to check if hospital hospitalization/disability duration qualifies it as grievous under statutory 20-day rule.

steps.title: Recording of Victim & Eyewitness Statements u/s 180 BNSS
steps.description: Examine the injured victim (once certified medically fit to speak) and all eyewitnesses. Record comprehensive statements under BNSS Section 180 (formerly Section 161 CrPC). Document the exact sequence of events, identity of assailants, specific weapons wielded by each accused, and underlying motive (property dispute, enmity, sudden quarrel).
required_evidence: Section 180 BNSS written statement of the injured victim detailing the assault and identifying assailants
Section 180 BNSS statements of independent eyewitnesses, bystanders, and first responders
Audio-video recordings of witness examinations (where applicable under BNSS)
steps.condition_to_start: Victim medically stabilized and witnesses identified from spot.
steps.condition_to_complete: Comprehensive witness testimony compiled establishing individual roles and weapon usage of each accused.
if_blocked: If the victim's speech is impaired due to facial/jaw fractures, record statement via written answers or gestures in the presence of an independent medical officer.

steps.title: Crime Scene Examination & Physical Exhibit Seizure
steps.description: Inspect the assault spot under BNSS Section 176(3) (or standard crime scene protocols). Lift liquid bloodstains, blood-stained earth, control earth, torn clothing, or weapons/instruments left behind by assailants (iron rods, wooden lathis, knives, bricks). Prepare spot sketch map and panchnama.
required_evidence: Seizure memos for bloodstains, weapons, and torn garments found at spot
Spot inspection sketch map and photographic log of the assault location
Forensic spot examination report
steps.condition_to_start: Assault location secured by investigating police team.
steps.condition_to_complete: Physical exhibits lifted, sealed with official seal, labeled, and dispatched to FSL.
if_blocked: If the assault occurred inside a private residence or commercial shop, seize internal access logs and CCTV records under Section 94 BNSS.

steps.title: Weapon Seizure & Forensic Compatibility Examination
steps.description: Recover the weapons used in the assault (either from crime scene, upon arrest, or pursuant to accused disclosure). Submit seized weapons alongside the hospital MLC report to the forensic medical officer / FSL under Section 94/329 BNSS for expert opinion on whether the specific grievous injuries documented on the victim could be caused by the seized weapons.
required_evidence: Seizure memo of dangerous weapons / blunt or sharp instruments
Surgeon's / FSL Weapon Compatibility Expert Report matching weapon shape/dimensions to victim wound patterns
FSL Serological report confirming presence of victim's blood on recovered weapons
steps.condition_to_start: Weapons recovered by investigating team.
steps.condition_to_complete: Weapons medically and scientifically linked to the victim's grievous injuries.
if_blocked: If the weapon is a common domestic or agricultural tool (axe, sickle, pestle), distinguish it from household items by testing for microscopic blood/epithelial traces in crevices at FSL.

steps.title: CCTV Surveillance & Telecom Enmity Tracing
steps.description: Requisition CCTV footage from private establishments, housing societies, or municipal cameras covering the assault location under BNSS Section 94 to visually confirm the aggression. Simultaneously issue notices to TSPs for CDRs and Cell ID locations of suspects and victim to verify presence and prior disputes.
required_evidence: CCTV video footage capturing the physical assault and weapon wielding
Section 63 BSA electronic admissibility certificates for video media
Telecom CDRs and cell tower geolocation mapping reports
steps.condition_to_start: Surveillance cameras or mobile phones identified at the scene.
steps.condition_to_complete: Video surveillance media and telecom tracking logs procured and certified.
if_blocked: If CCTV is hosted on cloud servers operated by non-telecom ISPs, route Section 94 notices through entity_id isp_non_telecom.

steps.title: Arrest of Accused, Custody Remand & Medical Profiling
steps.description: Arrest the assailant under BNSS Section 35. Conduct immediate medical examination under BNSS Section 51/53 to document any mutual altercation injuries and draw blood/reference samples. If weapons or blood-stained clothes are hidden, produce accused before Magistrate to secure police custody remand under BNSS Section 187 for recovery under Section 23 BSA.
required_evidence: Arrest memo, personal search memo, and medical inspection report of accused
Voluntary disclosure statement leading to recovery of weapon or blood-stained clothes under Section 23 BSA
Magistrate's order granting police custody remand under Section 187 BNSS
steps.condition_to_start: Evidentiary linkage established against suspect.
steps.condition_to_complete: Accused arrested, medically profiled, biological samples drawn, and weapon recovery finalized.
if_blocked: If multiple accused participated in a mob assault, invoke Section 3(5) BNS (common intention) or Section 190 BNS (unlawful assembly) in the arrest memos to assign joint criminal liability.

steps.title: Legal Synthesis & Final Charge-Sheet Filing
steps.description: Ensure all radiological reports (X-rays/CT scans) and doctor certifications explicitly classifying the injury as 'Grievous Hurt' under BNS Section 116 are placed in the file. Assemble all FSL reports, witness statements, and recovery memos. File the final chargesheet under BNSS Section 193 specifying BNS Section 117 (Grievous hurt) or Section 118 (Grievous hurt by dangerous weapons).
required_evidence: Comprehensive police chargesheet under BNSS Section 193 specifying BNS Section 117/118
Certified MLC report, radiological films, and expert wound classification certificates
All FSL serological and weapon compatibility reports admissible under BNSS Section 329
Judicial cognizance order from the trial court
steps.condition_to_start: Investigation completed, accused remanded, and medical/forensic reports received.
steps.condition_to_complete: Charge-sheet formally submitted and accepted by the jurisdictional court within statutory timelines.
if_blocked: If the hospital delays issuing the final wound certificate due to ongoing outpatient orthopedic treatment, file the primary chargesheet with provisional MLC and submit final disability certificate u/s 193(9) BNSS.

dead_end_strategies.condition: Assault occurred during a unmonitored neighborhood or agrarian property dispute with mutual rioting, both sides suffered injuries, and cross-complaints (counter-FIRs) have been filed with partisan witnesses.
suggested_actions: Conduct independent investigation of both cross-cases simultaneously by the same IO as per Supreme Court jurisprudence (Nathi Lal v. State of UP) to determine which party was the aggressor.

Examine the nature, location, and severity of wounds documented in the hospital MLC reports of both sides: defensive wounds (forearms/palms) vs. offensive primary impact wounds (head/torso) scientifically identify the defending party.

Subpoena historical land records, revenue mutation entries under entity_id sub_registrar_property, or prior preventive litigation (107/116 CrPC / BNSS) to establish who held peaceful physical possession of the disputed property when aggression occurred.

title: Standard Operating Procedure for Investigation of Dowry Death Cases
source: Synthesized from BPR&D Investigation Guidelines for Dowry Death, BNSS 2023, Dowry Prohibition Act 1961, and MHA Advisories

steps.title: FIR Registration & Immediate Intimation to Executive Magistrate
steps.description: Upon receipt of information regarding the unnatural death (burns, bodily injury, hanging, poisoning) of a woman within 7 years of marriage, immediately register FIR under BNSS Section 173 (BNS Section 80; formerly IPC Section 304B) read with Section 498A IPC / BNS Section 85 and Dowry Prohibition Act. In strict compliance with BNSS Section 194/196 (formerly CrPC Section 174/176), immediately send special intimation to the jurisdictional Executive Magistrate / Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) to conduct statutory inquest proceedings. Note: Local police station / first responder unit is not present in the registry, hence department_entity_id is set to null.
required_evidence: Copy of recorded FIR under BNS Section 80 read with Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act
Written dispatch receipt of immediate intimation sent to Executive Magistrate / SDM
Marriage certificate, wedding invitation card, or municipal marriage registration proving marriage occurred within 7 years
steps.condition_to_start: Report of unnatural death of a married woman occurring within 7 years of her marriage.
steps.condition_to_complete: FIR registered, marriage duration statutorily verified, and Executive Magistrate formally requisitioned.
if_blocked: If the husband/in-laws attempt to secretly cremate or dispose of the body before police arrival, deploy armed police teams immediately to halt cremation and seize the corpse under Section 106 BNSS.

steps.title: Statutory Executive Magistrate Inquest Proceedings u/s 196 BNSS
steps.description: Under BNSS Section 196 (formerly CrPC Section 176), the inquest of a woman dying unnaturally within 7 years of marriage MUST be conducted by the Executive Magistrate / SDM (or Judicial Magistrate in custodial cases). Assist the Magistrate in conducting the inquest at the spot or morgue in the presence of the deceased's parents/relatives. Document exact posture, burn patterns, ligature marks, and defense wounds.
required_evidence: Statutory Executive Magistrate Inquest Report (Panchnama) recorded u/s 196 BNSS
Statements of deceased's parents, brothers, and blood relatives recorded during inquest by the Magistrate
High-resolution photographic and videographic recording of the inquest proceedings
steps.condition_to_start: Executive Magistrate arrives at crime scene or hospital morgue.
steps.condition_to_complete: Inquest finalized and signed by Executive Magistrate and blood relatives of the deceased.
if_blocked: If the Executive Magistrate is unavailable due to unavoidable administrative exigency, the IO must conduct police inquest u/s 194 BNSS in the presence of two independent panchas and deceased's parents, while recording reasons for Magistrate absence.

steps.title: Panel Doctor Post-Mortem Autopsy & Mandatory Video Recording
steps.description: Submit a formal requisition under BNSS Section 194 to the Chief Medical Officer (CMO) to conduct post-mortem examination by a Board of Doctors (Panel of at least two medical officers, including a female doctor or forensic expert). In accordance with NHRC and MHA guidelines for dowry deaths, the entire autopsy procedure MUST be videographed from start to finish. Request specific opinion on ante-mortem vs. post-mortem burns/hanging, cause of death, and preservation of viscera.
required_evidence: Certified Panel Medico-Legal Post-Mortem Autopsy Report signed by Board of Doctors
Unedited video recording of the complete autopsy procedure on digital storage media
Sealed containers containing preserved viscera, blood, stomach contents, and skin tags with doctor's specimen seal
steps.condition_to_start: Corpse delivered to hospital morgue along with SDM Inquest report.
steps.condition_to_complete: Autopsy completed by medical board under videography, cause of death certified, and sealed exhibits handed over to police.
if_blocked: If the panel autopsy reveals signs of homicidal strangulation disguised as suicidal hanging (e.g., fracture of hyoid bone, continuous horizontal ligature mark), immediately alter investigative trajectory to premeditated Murder (BNS Section 103).

steps.title: Forensic Crime Scene Examination & Physical Exhibit Seizure
steps.description: Summon the State FSL scientific team under BNSS Section 176(3). Thoroughly inspect the matrimonial home / room where death occurred. In burn cases: seize kerosene/petrol stove, fuel containers, matchboxes, burnt fabric, and control floor flooring to test for accelerants. In hanging cases: seize ceiling fan, ligature material (rope/sari), and stool/table; check for knot types and fiber transfers. In poisoning cases: seize medicine bottles, utensils, and vomit traces.
required_evidence: Seizure memos for accelerant containers, burnt garments, ligatures, matchboxes, and chemical residues
High-resolution scene photographs, videography, and spot sketch map
FSL scientific scene inspection report confirming presence or absence of forced entry or struggle
steps.condition_to_start: Matrimonial crime scene secured and sealed by investigating police team.
steps.condition_to_complete: All physical, chemical, and trace exhibits scientifically lifted, packaged, sealed with official seal, and forwarded to FSL.
if_blocked: If the in-laws washed or scrubbed the room prior to police arrival to destroy kerosene or poison traces, immediately register additional charges for destruction of evidence under BNS Section 238 (formerly Section 201 IPC).

steps.title: Recording Statements of Deceased's Parents & Relatives u/s 180/183 BNSS
steps.description: Examine the parents, siblings, relatives, and neighbors of the deceased. Record detailed statements under BNSS Section 180. To secure un-tampered evidentiary value, sponsor applications before the Magistrate to record judicial statements of the parents and key relatives under BNSS Section 183 (formerly Section 164 CrPC). Focus strictly on establishing statutory ingredients: specific demands for dowry (cash, car, gold, property), specific instances of cruelty/harassment, and proof that such cruelty occurred 'soon before her death'.
required_evidence: Section 180 BNSS written statements of parents, siblings, and independent neighborhood witnesses
Certified copy of Section 183 BNSS judicial statements of parents recorded by Magistrate
Letters, SMS, WhatsApp chats, audio recordings, or diary entries written by the deceased detailing dowry harassment
steps.condition_to_start: Parents and blood relatives of the deceased available for examination.
steps.condition_to_complete: Comprehensive witness testimony compiled establishing dowry cruelty 'soon before death' and Section 183 statements procured.
if_blocked: If parents reside in a distant state, utilize BNSS provisions permitting audio-video electronic examination or coordinate through local jurisdictional police to record depositions.

steps.title: Financial Tracing of Dowry Transactions, Bank Transfers & Property
steps.description: Investigate the financial trail of dowry demands and payments. Issue Section 94 BNSS notices to banks for account statements of the deceased's parents showing large cash withdrawals, RTGS/NEFT transfers, or cheque payments made to the husband/in-laws. Query bank lockers and sub-registrar offices under entity_id sub_registrar_property to trace real estate, vehicles, or gold ornaments transferred as dowry or demanded prior to death. Seize Stridhan property under Section 106 BNSS.
required_evidence: Certified bank statements of parents showing money transfers or cash withdrawals corresponding to wedding/dowry dates
Bank statements of husband and in-laws showing receipt of funds or unexplained deposits
Invoices/receipts for gold jewelry, vehicles, or consumer durables purchased by parents for in-laws
Seizure memo / inventory of recovered Stridhan (gold jewelry, gifts) from the matrimonial home or bank lockers
steps.condition_to_start: Specific dowry demands or financial transactions alleged in parental statements.
steps.condition_to_complete: Financial ledgers procured, bank transfers documented, and Stridhan property seized/inventoried.
if_blocked: If dowry was paid entirely in unaccounted cash without receipts, substantiate the transaction by examining wedding expenditure ledgers, marriage hall bookings, and jeweler witness statements.

steps.title: Telecom CDR & Digital Communication History Analysis
steps.description: Issue Section 94 BNSS notices to TSPs for Call Detail Records (CDRs), SMS logs, and Cell ID locations of the deceased, husband, and in-laws covering the 6 months prior to death. Analyse communication frequency and tower locations to establish who was present in the house at the time of death. Requisition IP logs and cloud backups from messaging platforms (WhatsApp/Email) to recover threatening messages or distress communications sent by the deceased.
required_evidence: CDRs and cell tower geolocation mapping reports confirming presence of husband/in-laws at matrimonial home during death window
Screenshots and certified export logs of SMS, WhatsApp chats, or emails showing dowry demands or distress complaints
Section 63 BSA electronic admissibility certificates from TSP nodal officers and platform compliance desks
steps.condition_to_start: Mobile phone numbers of deceased, husband, and in-laws identified.
steps.condition_to_complete: Telecom tracking logs and digital communication archives procured and certified under Section 63 BSA.
if_blocked: If the deceased's phone was broken or formatted by in-laws post-death, submit the physical handset to FSL / State Cyber CID for advanced chip-off memory extraction and data carving.

steps.title: FSL Toxicological, Chemical & Histopathological Report Requisition
steps.description: In compliance with BNSS Section 329, forward all sealed viscera samples, blood, burnt clothing, accelerant residues, or hanging ligatures to the State FSL / CFSL through a secure Road Certificate. In poisoning cases: requisition chemical screening for organic/inorganic poisons (pesticides, cyanide, arsenic). In burn cases: requisition chemical analysis confirming presence of kerosene/petrol hydrocarbons on clothing and skin. In hanging cases: requisition microscopic examination of ligature fibers and skin tissue.
required_evidence: Official forwarding letter addressed to Director FSL / CFSL detailing the specific chemical/toxicological questionnaire
Copy of Road Certificate (RC) and Malkhana register entry proving intact chain of custody
Certified FSL Toxicological / Chemical Analysis Report admissible under BNSS Section 329
FSL Serological / Physical comparison report for hanging ligatures and burnt fabric
steps.condition_to_start: Sealed viscera, medical exhibits, and scene exhibits gathered in station malkhana.
steps.condition_to_complete: Exhibits formally accepted by FSL and definitive chemical/toxicological analysis reports delivered to IO.
if_blocked: If FSL toxicological analysis is delayed beyond 60 days, obtain an expedited prioritization endorsement from the monitoring DCP/SP citing statutory gravity of dowry death.

steps.title: Arrest of Husband & Implicated In-Laws, Custody & Interrogation
steps.description: Upon establishing statutory ingredients (death within 7 years, unnatural cause, cruelty soon before death for dowry), arrest the husband and specifically implicated in-laws under BNSS Section 35. Ensure strict adherence to arrest guidelines (avoiding indiscriminate arrest of distant, non-resident relatives without specific evidence as cautioned by Supreme Court in Arnesh Kumar / Social Action Forum). Conduct medical examination under BNSS Section 51. Produce accused before Magistrate for custody remand.
required_evidence: Arrest memos, personal search memos, and medical examination reports of husband and implicated in-laws
Specific evidentiary justification memorandum in case diary proving direct involvement of each arrested relative
Magistrate's order granting judicial or police custody remand under Section 187 BNSS
Seizure memo of any Stridhan or dowry items recovered during police custody interrogation
steps.condition_to_start: Evidentiary linkage established against husband and specific co-residing in-laws via statements, CDRs, and financial trails.
steps.condition_to_complete: Accused lawfully arrested, medically profiled, and remanded to judicial/police custody.
if_blocked: If accused in-laws apply for anticipatory bail, strongly oppose before Sessions/High Court by presenting Section 183 parent statements, FSL chemical reports, and financial dowry trails.

steps.title: Legal Synthesis, Statutory Presumption Invocation & Final Charge-Sheet Filing
steps.description: Synthesize all evidentiary strands: marriage within 7 years, panel autopsy video, SDM inquest, FSL chemical/viscera report, parental Section 183 statements, bank transfer ledgers, and CDR presence logs. In the final chargesheet compiled under BNSS Section 193, explicitly invoke the mandatory legal presumption of Dowry Death under Section 118 BSA (formerly Section 113B Evidence Act) — which mandates that when cruelty soon before death for dowry is shown, the court SHALL presume that the accused caused the dowry death. File the chargesheet before the competent court within statutory timelines.
required_evidence: Comprehensive police chargesheet under BNSS Section 193 specifying BNS Section 80 (Dowry Death) read with Section 85 (Cruelty) and Sections 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act
Complete list of relied-upon documents: SDM Inquest, Panel Autopsy video, FSL chemical reports, Section 183 statements, bank ledgers, and CDRs
Specific legal memorandum in charge-sheet invoking mandatory statutory presumption under Section 118 Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA)
Formal judicial order taking cognizance of the charge-sheet by the Sessions Court
steps.condition_to_start: All investigative steps executed, accused remanded, and FSL/medical expert reports received.
steps.condition_to_complete: Charge-sheet formally submitted and accepted by the Sessions Court within statutory timelines.
if_blocked: If FSL viscera reports face administrative delay near the 90-day statutory limit, file the primary chargesheet with SDM inquest, panel autopsy, and Section 183 statements to invoke Section 118 BSA presumption, and file the viscera report later u/s 193(9) BNSS.

dead_end_strategies.condition: Deceased died of burn injuries in the kitchen, husband/in-laws claim it was an accidental stove burst, there are no eyewitnesses inside the house, and in-laws have sanitized the physical scene.
suggested_actions: Requisition the mechanical and chemical examination of the stove, cylinder, and regulator by FSL physics/chemical experts under BNSS Section 176(3): scientific distinction between a genuine mechanical stove blast (outward metal tearing, uniform soot) versus deliberate kerosene pouring (localized splash burn patterns on floor/body without stove rupture) conclusively exposes staged accidents.

Examine the exact burn injury distribution documented in the panel autopsy report: accidental kitchen burns predominantly affect front lower extremities and hands with splash marks, whereas homicidal immolation shows circumferential deep burns on back, scalp, and torso with defensive posturing.

Analyse the delay timeline between the fire occurrence, hospital admission, and police intimation: unexplained delays by in-laws in seeking emergency medical aid or taking the victim to a distant private facility instead of the nearest burn unit serve as strong circumstantial evidence of culpable mens rea under Section 6 BSA (conduct subsequent to fact).
